mechanisms.name: Aider repo map: tree-sitter tags + personalized PageRank + token-budget binary search, disk-cached by mtime
mechanisms.what: Aider parses every file with tree-sitter tags.scm queries into definitions/references, builds a networkx MultiDiGraph (files as nodes, identifier references as weighted edges), runs PageRank personalized toward the files in chat, then binary-searches how many ranked tags fit --map-tokens (default 1k). Edge weight multipliers in repomap.py: referenced in chat files x50, in mentioned_idents x10, long snake/camelCase identifiers (>=8 chars) x10, private (_prefix) x0.1, defined in >5 files x0.1; reference counts are square-rooted. Tags are cached in a versioned diskcache dir (.aider.tags.cache.v{N}) keyed by filename with the file mtime; a cache hit is `val.get('mtime') == file_mtime`. Refresh modes: auto (cache the rendered map only if map_processing_time > 1.0 s), always, files, manual. Token counting samples every Nth line for text >=200 chars and extrapolates. With no files in chat the budget is multiplied by --map-multiplier-no-files (default 2).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Gives the model whole-repo awareness ("GPT can see classes, methods and function signatures from everywhere in the repo. This alone may give it enough context to solve many tasks.") at a fixed token cost, and the mtime cache plus the >1 s heuristic keep per-turn overhead near zero on unchanged repos. Aider also warns that "Above about 25k tokens of context, most models start to become distracted", so a bounded map replaces dumping files.
mechanisms.evidence: Docs (fetched 2026-09-21): "a graph ranking algorithm, computed on a graph where each source file is a node and edges connect files which have dependencies"; "--map-tokens ... defaults to 1k tokens"; options page: "--map-refresh ... Options: auto, always, files, manual (default: auto)", "--map-multiplier-no-files ... (default: 2)". repomap.py (fetched 2026-09-21): TAGS_CACHE_DIR = f".aider.tags.cache.v{CACHE_VERSION}"; mul *= 50 for chat-file references; nx.pagerank(G, weight="weight", personalization=personalization, dangling=personalization); binary search between 0 and num_tags with initial middle = min(int(max_map_tokens // 25), num_tags), accept when pct_err < 0.15; "auto" caches when map_processing_time > 1.0.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Direct fit for the context stage (src/loop/stages/context.ts: <=300 code-prefiltered candidates, one Noul per candidate, 12-file/60 KB cap). Code builds the ranked map (no Jev, no LLM on this path) and Jev only ranks/selects from the PageRank-ordered shortlist, so Jev stays advisory. Implement in src/workspace/candidates.ts with a JSON cache keyed by path+mtime under the run scratch dir and the >1 s rebuild heuristic; personalize toward files named in the task text and the ledger's `fix <test> in <path>` items. RESEARCH.md §3.2 already lists the repo map as a to-adopt item; this adds the weights, cache and refresh details. [inference] a TypeScript tags pass without tree-sitter can use regex export/def scanning for TS/JS/Python first and stay within the < 50 ms per-step overhead budget only if cached.

mechanisms.name: Aider edit formats: per-model SEARCH/REPLACE (diff), diff-fenced, udiff, whole; fall back to whole on repeated edit failures
mechanisms.what: Aider ships several edit formats and picks one per model: `diff` (merge-conflict-style SEARCH/REPLACE blocks), `diff-fenced` (path inside the fence, for Gemini), `udiff` (simplified unified diff, used for GPT-4 Turbo to curb lazy coding), `whole` (full file), and streamlined `editor-diff`/`editor-whole` for architect mode. On failed edits it does not silently retry the same thing: it reports "Failed to apply edit to <filename>", tolerates "almost" correctly formatted blocks, and the documented remedy is to switch to `--edit-format whole`, `/clear` history, or use a stronger model.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: "the model only needs to return parts of the file which have changes" (diff/udiff) versus whole which "can be slow and costly because the LLM has to return the entire file"; udiff "reduced their 'lazy coding' tendencies". Matching the format to the model is the main lever on edit-apply reliability, and whole is the always-works fallback.
mechanisms.evidence: Edit-formats page (fetched 2026-09-21): whole = "The LLM is instructed to return a full, updated copy of each source file that needs changes"; diff = "a series of search/replace blocks. This is an efficient format"; diff-fenced "is primarily used with the Gemini family of models, which often fail to conform to the fencing approach"; udiff "was mainly used to the GPT-4 Turbo family of models, because it reduced their 'lazy coding' tendencies". Troubleshooting page: "Weaker models are more prone to disobeying the system prompt instructions"; "Run aider with --edit-format whole if were using a different edit format"; "Above about 25k tokens of context, most models start to become distracted".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's propose_action tool (src/loop/stages/propose.ts, src/provider/actions.ts, src/workspace/edit.ts and patch.ts) already carries edit/write/patch kinds; adopt the per-provider default (search/replace for Anthropic/OpenRouter Claude, diff-fenced for Gemini models once that provider lands, whole for weak/cheap generators) as a code-owned table in src/provider/prompts.ts, and add the aider escalation rule: two consecutive EditError/PatchError on the same file -> re-ask in `whole` for that file rather than repeating the format. Jev is not on this path; the loop detector's patchContentHash already sees repeats. RESEARCH.md §8.1-8.2 covers the action schema; this adds the fallback ladder and the Gemini fence caveat.

mechanisms.name: Aider architect/editor split: a reasoning model proposes, a cheap editor model writes the edits
mechanisms.what: Architect mode sends the request to the main model "to propose how to solve your coding request", then sends "another request to an 'editor model', asking it to turn the architect's proposal into specific file editing instructions" using editor-diff or editor-whole. `--architect`, `--editor-model`, `--editor-edit-format`, `--auto-accept-architect` (default True) control it.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: "the model has to split its attention between solving the coding problem and conforming to the edit format"; separating them "significantly improved the benchmark scores of many models, compared to their previous 'solo' baseline" (Claude 3.5 Sonnet 77.4% -> 80.5%, GPT-4o 71.4% -> 75.2%; o1-preview + DeepSeek/o1-mini 85% SOTA). The editor can be chosen on "cost, speed and code editing skill". Caveat in the same post: the top pairs "are therefore quite slow, so probably not practical for interactive use".
mechanisms.evidence: Architect post (fetched 2026-09-21): "Using o1-preview as the Architect with either DeepSeek or o1-mini as the Editor produced the SOTA score of 85%"; "Using the Architect/Editor approach also significantly improved the benchmark scores of many models"; modes page: "An architect model will propose changes and an editor model will translate that proposal into specific file edits"; options page: "--auto-accept-architect Enable/disable automatic acceptance of architect changes (default: True)", "--editor-model ... (default depends on --model)".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Maps onto jev+llm mode's single Provider interface: let the generator (e.g. Claude Sonnet 5 or GLM 5.3 Flash) act as architect emitting a plan-shaped proposal, and route the concrete edit to a cheaper/faster editor model (a second `Provider` instance selected by config `editor.provider/model`) in editor-whole for files under ~16 KB and editor-diff otherwise. Jev keeps its existing risk/judge/complete stages over the resulting proposal and is never the editor. In jev-only mode the synthesizer (src/synth) already plays architect with code, so this is a jev+llm-only knob. Keep --auto-accept semantics off by default in the TUI (the Jev risk verdict is the gate), on for --plain pipes. [inference] The speed win is when the editor is much cheaper than the architect; with a single fast model it is a net extra round-trip.

mechanisms.name: Aider auto-lint / auto-test after every edit, then auto-commit
mechanisms.what: After each set of edits Aider lints the edited files (default on, built-in linters for popular languages or `--lint-cmd`, including per-language `"language: cmd"`), optionally runs `--test-cmd` when `--auto-test` is on, and feeds non-zero-exit output back to the LLM to fix. Each LLM change is auto-committed (`--auto-commits` default True, `--dirty-commits` default True) so every step is git-reversible.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Cheap, deterministic, code-owned verification runs before any further model call, catching syntax/format breakage immediately; auto-commits make undo a `git` operation rather than a model task. Formatters must exit zero after fixing, so Aider recommends wrapping them to run twice.
mechanisms.evidence: Lint/test page (fetched 2026-09-21): aider will "automatically lint and test your code every time it makes changes"; lint command should "accept the filenames of the files to lint" and "return a non-zero exit code" on errors; test command should "print them on stdout/stderr and return a non-zero exit code". Options page: "--auto-lint ... (default: True)", "--auto-test ... (default: False)", "--auto-commits ... (default: True)", "--dirty-commits ... (default: True)".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's judge is already code on `run` steps in llm-jev (src/loop/stages/judge.ts: codeJudge from parsed counts) and the synthesizer verifies with tests; the missing piece is an automatic post-edit lint/typecheck step owned by code in src/loop/stages/execute.ts (e.g. `tsc --noEmit -p` scoped, `ruff`/`pyflakes`, or a configured lint-cmd) whose non-zero output is attached to the step's `executed` state before Jev's judge/complete Nouls. This shrinks Jev/LLM calls per accepted patch and never puts Jev on the verification path. Per-step git checkpoints already exist (src/checkpoint, src/undo); Aider's dirty-commits default argues for committing even when the tree started dirty, with the run id in the message.

mechanisms.name: Aider prompt caching with stable prefix ordering and keepalive pings
mechanisms.what: With `--cache-prompts`, Aider orders the request so the cacheable prefix is stable: system prompt, read-only files (`--read`/`/read-only`), the repository map, then editable files; the conversation follows. `--cache-keepalive-pings N` pings every 5 minutes to keep the provider cache warm (Anthropic keeps a cache 5 minutes by default).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Reuses the expensive static prefix across turns for "cost savings and faster coding"; the keepalive avoids paying the full prefix again after an idle gap. Caching stats are only visible with --no-stream.
mechanisms.evidence: Caching page (fetched 2026-09-21): cached components are "The system prompt", "Read only files added with --read or /read-only", "The repository map", "The editable files that have been added to the chat"; "By default, Anthropic keeps your cache for 5 minutes"; "--cache-keepalive-pings N ... ping every 5 minutes to keep the cache warm"; "caching statistics and costs are not available when streaming responses". Options page: "--cache-prompts Enable caching of prompts (default: False)", "--cache-keepalive-pings VALUE ... (default: 0)".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: For the generator only (src/provider/anthropic.ts, openrouter.ts): build the messages as [system, repo map, selected files, then the sliding window] so the prefix is byte-stable between steps, and mark cache breakpoints where the provider supports them. Jev requests are small state+questions payloads and are not the caching target. Keepalive pings spend money while idle, so make them off by default and only on in the TUI while a run is paused (docs/COORDINATION-DESIGN.md §7 pause points) with a visible cost line. [inference] Since JevCode streams, cache-hit accounting must come from the usage fields in the final SSE event, not from a non-stream call.

mechanisms.name: Codex sandbox/approval split: sandbox_mode decides what can happen, approval_policy decides when to ask; failures inside the sandbox escalate to an approval
mechanisms.what: Codex has three sandbox modes, `read-only`, `workspace-write` ("read files, edit within the workspace, and run routine local commands inside that boundary"), and `danger-full-access`, enforced by Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap or a bundled helper on Linux/WSL2, and a native sandbox on Windows; network is off by default. Approval policy is separate: `on-request` ("The model decides when to ask the user for approval"), `never` ("Failures are immediately returned to the model, and never escalated to the user for approval"), `granular` (per-category allow/auto-reject), with `untrusted` retired. In the protocol, WorkspaceWrite carries `writable_roots`, `network_access`, `exclude_tmpdir_env_var`, `exclude_slash_tmp`, and each WritableRoot has `read_only_subpaths` plus `protected_metadata_names` ("must not be created or replaced under root unless the policy grants an explicit write rule"), which is how .git/.codex are protected inside a writable workspace. The Auto preset is `--sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval on-request`.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: The agent runs freely inside a mechanically enforced boundary and only pauses when it actually hits the wall, so routine commands never prompt; "Approvals determine when Codex pauses before an action, while the sandbox determines which files and network resources commands can access." `never` gives a fully non-interactive mode where a sandbox denial is just tool output for the model to route around.
mechanisms.evidence: Sandboxing page (fetched 2026-09-21): read-only "The agent can inspect files, but it can't edit files or run commands without approval"; danger-full-access "removes the filesystem and network boundaries"; "It asks before using the internet or going beyond the workspace boundary"; macOS uses "the built-in Seatbelt framework"; Linux requires bubblewrap or "a bundled helper". Approvals page: Auto = `--sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval on-request`; `untrusted` "(retired): No longer supported". protocol.rs doc comments: OnRequest "The model decides when to ask the user for approval."; Never "Never ask the user to approve commands. Failures are immediately returned to the model, and never escalated to the user for approval."; WorkspaceWrite "Same as ReadOnly but additionally grants write access to the current working directory"; WritableRoot.protected_metadata_names doc quoted above. config_types.rs: SandboxMode has `#[default] ReadOnly` while the product docs call workspace-write the default preset (discrepancy noted).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts already runs `(allow default)` with writes and secret reads denied and an env allowlist (DESIGN.md §8). Adopt the Codex vocabulary as the user-facing `--sandbox read-only|workspace-write|full` (RESEARCH.md §4 adopt item 7 proposes exactly this) and add `protected_metadata_names`-style deny rules for `.git`, `.jevcode`, the config dir and `.env` inside the writable root. Keep Jev off the enforcement path: the seatbelt profile is code; Jev's risk stage (src/loop/stages/risk.ts, bands 0.3/0.7) is the on-request reviewer that decides whether a denied-by-sandbox action is escalated to the user or returned to the generator as a failed outcome. Map `--plain` pipes to Codex's `never` semantics (denials come back as ExecResult, prompts take the safe default), which the README already promises. Fix the mode-default ambiguity by pinning workspace-write in defaults.ts and documenting it.

mechanisms.name: Model-as-approval-reviewer: Codex `approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"` and Claude Code auto-mode classifier
mechanisms.what: Both harnesses put a second model in front of risky actions instead of the human. Codex: "When enabled via approvals_reviewer = "auto_review", eligible approval requests route through an automatic reviewer agent before execution, evaluating actions for data exfiltration, credential risks, and destructive operations", inside the same sandbox boundary as on-request. Claude Code auto mode: "A separate classifier model reviews actions before they run, blocking anything that escalates beyond your request, targets unrecognized infrastructure, or appears driven by hostile content Claude read"; the classifier trusts the working directory and the remotes configured at session start, presumes `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash drop` discard work, reviews `rm`/`rmdir` on critical paths even inside substitution, and also reviews SendMessage traffic between agents; a handful of critical paths are never auto-approved in any mode except bypassPermissions.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Removes routine prompts while keeping a review on every side-effecting action, so unattended and parallel runs do not stall; explicit hard rules (critical paths, ask rules) still override the model. Claude Code notes the classifier "adds model usage" and that a failed classifier request surfaces as "cannot determine the safety" rather than silently allowing.
mechanisms.evidence: Codex approvals page (fetched 2026-09-21): auto_review quote above; "This adds model usage but maintains the same sandbox boundary as standard on-request mode". Claude Code permission-modes page (fetched 2026-09-21): "In auto mode, a second model, the classifier, reviews actions instead of you"; "Explicit ask rules still force a prompt"; "The classifier trusts your working directory and the remotes that were configured for it when the session started. A remote added or repointed during the session ... isn't trusted"; "Writes to a small set of paths are never auto-approved, except in bypassPermissions mode"; a message saying auto mode "cannot determine the safety" means "a classifier request failed".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: This is precisely what JevCode's Jev risk stage already is (four one-quantity Scores + matches_intent Noul, risk = max over dimensions, verdict bands 0.3/0.7), so the lesson is the shape of the hard rules around the model rather than the model itself: add a code-owned never-auto-approve list (git history-destroying commands, rm on the workspace root/home, writes under .git and the config dir, remotes added mid-run) that bypasses Jev entirely, treat a failed/timeout Jev risk call as `ask` (or safe-default deny in --plain) rather than allow, and log the dimension and level text in the pane as it does today. Also apply the reviewer to inter-lane messages once COORDINATION-DESIGN.md §5 messaging lands. Jev remains advisory: it can only tighten (escalate) or release routine actions, never override the hard list.

mechanisms.name: Codex subagents: TOML-defined, spawned only on explicit request, inherit the parent's sandbox and approval mode, capped by [agents] thread limits
mechanisms.what: Subagents are TOML files in `~/.codex/agents/` or `.codex/agents/` with required `name`, `description`, `developer_instructions` and optional config keys (`model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `mcp_servers`). "Current local Codex releases delegate when you ask directly or when applicable AGENTS.md or skill instructions request it"; "Subagents inherit your current sandbox policy"; concurrency is capped by `[agents] max_concurrent_threads_per_session` (excludes the primary); "Codex handles orchestration across agents, including spawning new subagents, routing follow-up instructions, waiting for results, and closing agent threads."
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Parallel fan-out for independent work without letting the model silently multiply cost: spawning is explicit, threads are capped, and every child runs under the same mechanical boundary as the parent. The docs are blunt that "subagent workflows consume more tokens than comparable single-agent runs".
mechanisms.evidence: Subagents page (fetched 2026-09-21): required fields name/description/developer_instructions; "Ask Codex in an app chat to delegate independent parts of the work to subagents"; "Subagents inherit your current sandbox policy"; `max_concurrent_threads_per_session` caps concurrent spawned-agent threads; "Because each subagent does its own model and tool work, subagent workflows consume more tokens than comparable single-agent runs." [secondary, unverified] third-party posts (codex.danielvaughan.com, 2026-03-26) cite a default of 6 threads and keys `agents.max_threads`, `agents.max_depth`, `agents.job_max_runtime_seconds`; the official config-reference fetch was rate-limited and not retried.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: For COORDINATION-DESIGN.md §6 (sub-agent and lane coordination): make lane spawning explicit (a `/lanes` or `/split` command, or a Jev-confirmed `parallelizable` Noul with the user's yes), never implicit; store lane definitions as small JSON/TOML under `.jevcode/agents/`; child lanes inherit the parent's sandbox mode, budget slice and Jev provider; add `lanes.maxConcurrent` (default small, e.g. 4) and `lanes.maxDepth` (1) to src/config/defaults.ts with the spend module (src/spend) splitting the wall/cost budget. Jev decides which lane's result to take (a Choice with escape option) but never runs the lanes.

mechanisms.name: Claude Code subagents: isolated context windows, background by default, reduced tool set, concurrency and depth caps, resumable with full history
mechanisms.what: A subagent is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description` required; `tools`/`disallowedTools`, `model`, `permissionMode`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `memory`, `hooks`, `background`, `isolation: worktree`, `effort`, `omitClaudeMd`, `initialPrompt`). Non-fork subagents start with only their system prompt, the delegation message, CLAUDE.md hierarchy, a git status snapshot, preloaded skills and the sibling roster; forks inherit the parent conversation. In interactive fork mode subagents run in the background by default and "run with a smaller built-in tool set than foreground subagents"; permission prompts from a background subagent surface in the main session naming the asker. Limits: 20 concurrent (`Concurrent subagent limit reached`, "the error tells Claude not to retry"; `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`), three nesting layers (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`). Custom subagents are resumable via SendMessage with full history; `maxTurns` stops mark output as partial and say it can be continued.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: "Preserve context by keeping exploration and implementation out of your main conversation"; "the verbose output stays in the subagent's context while only the relevant summary returns". Background-by-default keeps the operator's composer free. Trade-off stated in the docs: "Latency matters. A subagent that isn't a fork starts fresh and may need time to gather context".
mechanisms.evidence: Sub-agents page (fetched 2026-09-21): "Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions."; "Foreground subagents block the main conversation until complete."; "Background subagents run concurrently while you continue working. When a background subagent reaches a tool call that needs permission, Claude Code surfaces the prompt in your main session and names the subagent that is asking."; "By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with Concurrent subagent limit reached"; "By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation."; "Resumed subagents retain their full conversation history"; "When a subagent stops at its maxTurns limit, Claude Code marks the returned output as partial". Model precedence: per-invocation `model` > frontmatter > `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` > main model.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Design the lane model (COORDINATION §6) so each lane is an Engine (src/loop/engine.ts createEngine) with its own sliding window (src/loop/window.ts), a tool allowlist expressed as permitted Action kinds, its own step/cost budget (maxTurns equivalent from src/loop/budget.ts) and a `partial` flag on its RunResult when the budget stops it; resume = the existing --resume checkpoint path (src/checkpoint) keyed by lane id. Surface lane permission prompts in the main TUI console with the lane name, exactly as Claude Code does, and route them through the same Jev risk stage. Cap concurrency and depth in config with a non-retryable error text so the generator does not loop. Jev's role is the per-lane judge/complete and the parent-level Choice among lane results; it does not orchestrate. Prefer a fork-style lane (inherits the parent window) for latency-sensitive splits, a fresh lane for verbose exploration.

mechanisms.name: Claude Code hooks: deterministic lifecycle enforcement via JSON-on-stdin, exit-code semantics, async hooks and PostToolBatch
mechanisms.what: Hooks fire on ~30 lifecycle events (SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, SubagentStart/Stop, TaskCreated/Completed, PreCompact/PostCompact, WorktreeCreate/Remove, PreModelSwitch, Stop, etc.). Handler types: `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt`, `agent`. Exit 0 = proceed (stdout parsed as JSON if it starts with `{` and ends with `}`); exit 2 = block ("even a JSON permissionDecision of "allow" can't override it"); other codes are non-blocking. PreToolUse JSON can return `permissionDecision` allow/deny/ask, `updatedInput`, `additionalContext`. Default timeouts 600 s (command/http/mcp_tool), 30 s (prompt), 60 s (agent), lowered on prompt-submit and message-display events. Command hooks support `async: true` (no blocking, no enforced timeout) and `asyncRewake: true` (wakes Claude on exit 2 with stderr as a system reminder). `PostToolBatch` fires "After a full batch of parallel tool calls resolves, before the next model call".
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Policy lives in code the user controls and runs the same way every time, with no model in the loop; async hooks keep formatters/loggers off the critical path; PostToolBatch runs one hook per model call instead of per tool call; a schema-invalid JSON result is a visible non-blocking error rather than a silent failure.
mechanisms.evidence: Hooks page (fetched 2026-09-21): PreToolUse "Before a tool call executes. Can block it"; PostToolBatch quote above; "Exit 2 means a blocking error. On events that can block, exit 2 blocks whether or not you print JSON"; "exit 0 with a parsed object that fails schema validation is a non-blocking error: the action proceeds, and the transcript shows a <hook name> hook error notice"; timeouts "Defaults: 600 for command, http, and mcp_tool; 30 for prompt; 60 for agent"; `async: true` "runs in the background without blocking"; `asyncRewake: true` "runs in the background and wakes Claude on exit code 2"; regex matchers use JavaScript RegExp.prototype.test.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: RESEARCH.md §4 adopt item 8 already commits to JSON-on-stdin hooks with exit 0/2 semantics. Add: (1) a `pre_action` hook point in src/loop/stages/execute.ts that can deny/ask/allow and rewrite the action (updatedInput), evaluated by code before Jev's risk stage so a hook deny short-circuits a paid Jev call; (2) `post_step` (per step, the PostToolBatch analogue) rather than per action, for lint/format/log hooks; (3) `async` hooks that run detached with their pid recorded in the checkpoint so pause/end can reap them; (4) fixed budgets: 600 s default clamped to remaining wall time via clampCommandTimeout. Hooks are code-owned and Jev never sees them except through the state they leave (e.g. lint output). Do not add prompt/agent hook types in v1: a model-evaluated hook is exactly the mission-critical placement Jev should avoid.

mechanisms.name: Claude Code background Bash tasks: Ctrl+B, task IDs, output to file, cleanup and caps
mechanisms.what: A running Bash tool call can be moved to the background with `Ctrl+B` (twice under tmux) or requested as a background command; "it runs the command asynchronously and immediately returns a background task ID" and the session keeps accepting prompts. Output is written to a file that can be read later; `/tasks` lists running shells and subagents (Ctrl+T is the to-do checklist, not the task view); tasks are cleaned up at exit (including setsid/timeout-detached processes on macOS/Linux), terminated if output exceeds 5 GB, and reaped under critical memory pressure after 30 idle minutes; commands owned by a foreground subagent end when it answers. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` turns it all off. In `-p` runs a background shell is terminated about five seconds after the final result.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Long test suites, dev servers and builds never block the composer; the model is notified when a task completes and reads only what it needs from the output file; caps and exit cleanup prevent orphaned processes and runaway logs.
mechanisms.evidence: Interactive-mode page (fetched 2026-09-21): "When Claude Code runs a command in the background, it runs the command asynchronously and immediately returns a background task ID. Claude Code can respond to new prompts while the command continues executing in the background."; "Press Ctrl+B to move a regular Bash tool invocation to the background. Tmux users must press Ctrl+B twice"; "Background tasks are automatically terminated if output exceeds 5GB"; "processes that detached from the task's shell, such as ones started under setsid or timeout, stop too"; memory-pressure reap "provided the session has been idle for at least 30 minutes and no turn or subagent is running". Headless page: "that shell is terminated about five seconds after Claude has returned its final result and stdin has closed".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: src/sandbox/run.ts already spawns detached process groups with a three-pass kill and rolling head/tail buffers (DESIGN.md §8), which is the hard part. Add a background variant: `Sandbox.runBackground()` returns a task id, streams to `<run>/tasks/<id>.log`, and emits `task:*` events so the TUI status line shows `⠹ 2 tasks` and a `/tasks` command lists/stops them; bind Ctrl-B in src/tui/keys/bindings.ts to background the current `run` action. Jev's judge then reads the tail/summary when the task ends (a `task_finished` step) rather than blocking the step. Cap by bytes on disk (JevCode's 200 KB head + 16 KB tail is already far tighter than 5 GB) and reap on session end via the existing kill.ts snapshot. Keep this out of --plain pipes (Codex/Claude both kill leftovers there) unless --json consumers ask for it.

mechanisms.name: Claude Code plan mode: read-only exploration with an explicit approval gate, cycled with Shift+Tab
mechanisms.what: Plan mode "tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them. Claude reads files, runs shell commands to explore, and writes a plan, but does not edit your source." Enter with `Shift+Tab`, a `/plan` prefix, or `claude --permission-mode plan`; the status bar shows `⏸ plan mode on`. Approving a plan exits plan mode into the permission mode the approve option names; "No, keep planning" stays. Shift+Tab cycles `default -> acceptEdits -> plan -> default` (optional `bypassPermissions`, `auto` slot in after plan). When auto mode is available and `useAutoModeDuringPlan` is on, the classifier reviews exploratory commands instead of prompting. `defaultMode: plan` in `.claude/settings.json` makes it the project default.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Separates thinking from acting so the operator reviews the shape of a change before any disk write, at the cost of one approval; the mode is visible in the status bar and one key away. Caveat: in interactive terminals with bypassPermissions available the blocks are not enforced, but they are kept in `-p`, SDK and VS Code contexts.
mechanisms.evidence: Permission-modes page (fetched 2026-09-21): plan mode definition quoted above; "Except in interactive terminal sessions with bypass permissions available, edits stay blocked until you approve the plan."; "Press Shift+Tab again to leave plan mode without approving a plan."; "Approving a plan exits plan mode and switches the session to the permission mode each approve option describes"; "From auto, the first press switches to default, and the cycle then runs default → acceptEdits → plan → back to default"; "Plan mode keeps its blocks wherever Claude Code runs without an interactive terminal". Common-workflows page: "The status bar shows ⏸ plan mode on while plan mode is active."
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode already has a plan object (src/loop/plan.ts, ledger items) and the rule that nothing runs until Jev reads a task; make that a visible mode: a `plan` badge in the console header alongside `jev-only`/`jev+llm`, a Shift-Tab (or Tab-cycle) binding in src/tui/keys that cycles `ask -> plan -> auto-accept-edits`, and a plan-approval bubble (`[y] run it [e] edit plan [n] keep planning`) before the first side-effecting step. In plan mode the engine allows only `read`/`run` of the code-owned read-only command set and the synthesizer's shadow test runs; Jev's `plan_still_valid` Noul (intent stage) and the completion stage stay as they are. Enforce the block in code for --plain/--json regardless of the interactive setting. This puts the human, not Jev, on the gate, which matches the harness-not-mission-critical requirement.

mechanisms.name: Claude Code worktrees: one checkout per parallel session or subagent, with locking, cleanup rules and mechanical isolation checks
mechanisms.what: `claude --worktree <name>` creates `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` on branch `worktree-<name>` (a generated name if omitted); `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tools move a running session; subagents get `isolation: worktree`. `worktree.baseRef` is `"fresh"` (default branch on the remote, fetch capped at 5 s if not fetched in 24 h) or `"head"`. `.worktreeinclude` (gitignore syntax) copies gitignored files such as `.env` into each new worktree. On exit a clean unnamed worktree is removed automatically, a named or dirty one prompts keep/remove; `-p` runs never clean up. "While an agent is running, Claude Code holds a git worktree lock on its worktree so that concurrent cleanup can't remove it"; a periodic sweep removes subagent/background worktrees older than `cleanupPeriodDays` unless they hold work, and releases locks left by dead processes. Isolation is enforced with four checks: edits targeting the main checkout are blocked, commands whose cwd resolves to the main checkout are blocked, git redirected into the main checkout (`git -C`, `--git-dir`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `cd`) is blocked, and commands whose shape cannot be verified (computed command names, `${!name}`) are blocked and Claude is told how to rewrite them. Worktrees share `.git`, project plugins and permission approvals (saved to the main checkout's settings.local.json).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Parallel edits cannot collide, cleanup is safe by construction (locks while running, never delete work), and the blocked-command rules are mechanical rather than model-judged. Requires at least one commit (`Failed to resolve base branch "HEAD"` otherwise).
mechanisms.evidence: Worktrees page (fetched 2026-09-21): "By default, the worktree is created under .claude/worktrees/<name>/ at your repository root, on a new branch named worktree-<name>"; baseRef "fresh" / "head" definitions; "Only files that match a pattern and are also gitignored are copied"; "Each subagent gets a temporary worktree that Claude Code removes automatically when the subagent finishes without changes"; lock sentence quoted above; "The sweep also releases a lock Claude Code set for a session whose process has exited"; the four checks under "How Claude Code enforces isolation"; "Non-interactive runs with -p have no exit prompt, so Claude doesn't clean up their worktrees"; "the repository needs at least one commit first" (common-workflows).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: For lanes and for the cross-device registry (COORDINATION §3-§4 leases): create `.jevcode/worktrees/<lane>/` via src/workspace/git.ts with `git worktree add -b jevcode/<lane>`, write a marker in the worktree's git metadata, hold `git worktree lock` while the lane's engine runs, and sweep by age only when `git status --porcelain` is empty and no unpushed commits exist. Copy `.env` into lanes via a `.worktreeinclude`-style list (JevCode already reads `./.env`, so without this a lane would lose its keys). Point the seatbelt writable root at the lane's worktree and deny the main checkout, which gives the Codex/Claude isolation checks for free at the OS level instead of by command parsing; add the `git -C`/`GIT_DIR` redirect check in code for the `run` action as a cheap second layer. Jev is not involved. Default baseRef `head` for lanes (they fix in-progress work), `fresh` for user-started parallel sessions.

mechanisms.name: Claude Code agent view: one screen for background sessions with states, peek/reply, stop, attach and PR labels; each background session auto-isolates in a worktree before its first edit
mechanisms.what: `claude agents` shows every background session grouped as Pinned / Ready for review / Needs input / Working / Completed, each row with a state icon, name, current activity or question, and age. Launch with a prompt in the dispatch input, `/bg "..."` or Left on an empty prompt from inside a session, or `claude --bg "..."`. Keys: Space peeks and lets you type a reply without attaching, Enter/Right attaches, Ctrl+T pins, Ctrl+R renames, Ctrl+X stops and a second press within 2 s deletes, Shift+Up/Down reorders, Ctrl+S regroups. "Before editing files, Claude moves the session into an isolated git worktree under .claude/worktrees/, so parallel sessions can read the same checkout but each writes to its own" (skipped if already in a linked worktree, not a git repo, or `worktree.bgIsolation: "none"`). Notifications fire when a session needs input, finishes or fails; "Session state persists on disk through auto-updates and supervisor restarts. Sessions are also preserved when your machine sleeps."
mechanisms.why_it_helps: The operator can dispatch many runs and only be interrupted by the ones that need input, answer them inline without context-switching, and trust that stopping is two keystrokes and that sleep/restart does not lose state.
mechanisms.evidence: Agent-view page (fetched 2026-09-21): "Agent view, opened with claude agents, is one screen for all your background sessions: what's running, what needs your input, and what's done."; "Each row shows the session's name, current activity, and its age, counted from when the session was created; a finished session's age freezes at how long the run took."; "Press Space on a selected row to open the peek panel ... Type a reply in the peek panel and press Enter to send it to that session."; worktree isolation sentence quoted above; "Each session uses your subscription quota independently"; persistence sentence quoted above.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode has `jevcode sessions list|reindex|prune|unlock` and `--list-sessions`; turn the list into an in-TUI overlay (src/tui/Overlay.tsx) with the same five states derived from the session registry and lease state (COORDINATION §3, §7 pause/resume/end), a peek panel that shows the last transcript lines and the pending `run this as a task?`/risk prompt, and keys: Space peek, Enter attach (`-c`/`--resume` path), Ctrl-X stop then delete, P pause at the next pause point. Show per-session spend from src/spend in the row (JevCode bills per key rather than per subscription). Pause/stop are code-owned (checkpoint first, as the exit-code table promises); Jev only classifies the row's 'needs input' text if the intent stage is already running. Persist across sleep by re-validating the lease on wake instead of treating the gap as idle.

mechanisms.name: Claude Code headless `-p` with `--bare`, structured output, unattended permission handling and resume-from-anywhere
mechanisms.what: `claude -p` runs one turn non-interactively; `--bare` skips "auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md" to reduce startup time and make CI runs identical across machines, never reads OAuth or the keychain, and is "the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls". `--output-format text|json|stream-json` (json includes `total_cost_usd`; stream-json is NDJSON whose last line is a `result` message, with `parent_tool_use_id` on subagent messages and `system/api_retry` retry events). `--permission-prompts none` denies anything that would prompt and tells Claude not to retry; `dontAsk` denies every prompt but keeps read-only commands. `--continue`/`--resume <id>` work from any directory and can take a transcript path. Background subagents keep `-p` open until done with a 10-minute idle ceiling (`CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`); SIGTERM exits 143 and leaves the turn unfinished, SIGINT ends the turn; stdin is capped at 10 MB.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Startup and determinism for scripts ("A hook in a teammate's ~/.claude or an MCP server in the project's .mcp.json won't run"), machine-readable cost and retry telemetry, explicit non-interactive denial semantics, and resumable multi-command pipelines.
mechanisms.evidence: Headless page (fetched 2026-09-21): "Add --bare to reduce startup time by skipping auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md."; "--bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release."; "With --output-format json, the response payload includes total_cost_usd"; "Anything that would prompt is denied unless a PermissionRequest hook allows it, Claude is told that nobody can approve the request and not to retry it"; "By default the wait ends after 10 minutes of continuous idle waiting"; "Claude Code exits with code 143" on SIGTERM; "Piped stdin is capped at 10MB"; `--resume` "finds the session by its ID in any project on the reference machine".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's `run --plain`/`--json` (NDJSON schema jevcode.events/1) and exit-code table are the equivalents. Adopt: a `--bare`-like fast path for pipes that skips config-dir discovery, `.env` scanning beyond the workspace, session indexing and completions/man lookups (the first-frame rule already defers these for the TUI; extend the same ordering to the plain runner and measure in src/perf/first-frame.ts); add `total_cost_usd`-style per-run cost and `jev_calls` counts to the final `result` event; make `--plain` denial semantics explicit (`--prompts none` = safe default, tell the generator not to retry, matching Codex `never`); document 143 on SIGTERM with checkpoint-first. Jev is unaffected: it is called the same way in both runners.

speed_tricks: Build the repo map in code and cache it: tags keyed by path+mtime on disk, the rendered map re-used unless the inputs changed or the last build took > 1 s (Aider `--map-refresh auto` heuristic, repomap.py); estimate tokens by sampling every Nth line and extrapolating rather than tokenizing whole files. Jev only ranks the PageRank-ordered shortlist, so the map is never a paid call. [https://aider.chat/2023/10/22/repomap.html, repomap.py]

Keep the map small by default (Aider: 1k tokens, x2 when no files are selected) instead of streaming file contents; Aider's own guidance is that models degrade above ~25k tokens of context, so a bounded map is both cheaper and more reliable. [https://aider.chat/docs/repomap.html, https://aider.chat/docs/troubleshooting/edit-errors.html]

Order generator prompts stable-prefix-first (system, repo map, read-only files, editable files, then the sliding window) so provider prompt caching hits every step; only add keepalive pings while a run is paused and show the cost. [https://aider.chat/docs/usage/caching.html]

Use search/replace (diff) edits by default and escalate to `whole` for a file only after two failed applies; never repeat the same failing format. Gemini-family models need the path inside the fence (diff-fenced). [https://aider.chat/docs/more/edit-formats.html]

In jev+llm mode, split architect and editor: the strong model proposes a plan-shaped change, a cheap fast model emits the edit in editor-whole/editor-diff; Aider reports +3 to +4 points for Sonnet/GPT-4o pairs and cautions the top pairs are too slow for interactive use, so pair a fast editor. [https://aider.chat/2024/09/26/architect.html]

Run a code-owned lint/typecheck on edited files immediately after each edit (Aider `--auto-lint` default True) and attach non-zero output to the step state; this catches breakage before any Jev judge or generator call. [https://aider.chat/docs/usage/lint-test.html]

Never pre-ask for routine actions: enforce the boundary mechanically (seatbelt writable root = workspace, network off, .git/.jevcode protected) and only escalate when an action hits the wall (Codex `on-request`); in pipes use Codex `never` semantics where denials return to the model as failed outcomes. [https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing, protocol.rs]

Background long commands: return a task id at once, stream output to a file under the run dir, notify on completion, bind Ctrl-B to background the current run action; cap by bytes and reap the process group on exit (Claude Code Ctrl+B, /tasks). [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode]

Give background lanes a reduced action set and their own window so verbose exploration never lands in the main transcript; cap concurrency (Claude Code 20) and depth (3) with a non-retryable error text so the generator does not spin. [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents]

Make hooks per step (Claude Code `PostToolBatch` = once per model call) and run formatters/loggers as `async` hooks detached from the critical path; a `pre_action` hook that denies short-circuits the Jev risk call entirely. [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks]

One worktree per lane with the sandbox writable root pointed at it: OS-level isolation replaces command-text parsing for most cases, and `git worktree lock` while running plus a status-clean sweep makes cleanup safe without prompts. Copy `.env` in via a `.worktreeinclude`-style list or the lane loses its keys. [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees]

Add a `--bare`-style fast path for `--plain/--json` runs that skips config-dir/session-index/completion discovery and never touches the keychain; Claude Code calls this the recommended mode for scripts and will make it the `-p` default. Emit per-run cost and Jev-call counts in the final NDJSON `result` line. [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless]

Spawn parallel lanes only on explicit request (Codex delegates "when you ask directly or when applicable AGENTS.md or skill instructions request it"), since subagent workflows "consume more tokens than comparable single-agent runs". [https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents]

Test small and iterate: use the existing `jevcode perf` first-frame/step-overhead gates (< 300 ms first frame, < 50 ms per-step overhead in DESIGN.md §8/§12) as the only regression checks for these changes rather than SWE-bench-scale runs, per the user's no-comprehensive-benchmarks instruction. [inference from repo docs]
pitfalls: Architect/editor top configurations are "quite slow, so probably not practical for interactive use" (Aider); with one fast model it is a pure extra round-trip. Only enable when the editor is materially cheaper/faster than the architect.

Context above ~25k tokens makes "most models ... less likely to conform to their system prompt" (Aider troubleshooting); a repo map plus selected files must stay under the existing 12-file/60 KB cap, not add to it.
Weak models disobey edit formats; Gemini often breaks the standard fence (needs diff-fenced). A per-provider format table is required, not one global format.
Aider caching stats are unavailable when streaming; with SSE, cache-hit accounting must come from the final usage event. Keepalive pings cost money every 5 minutes while idle.

Codex's protocol enum marks `read-only` as `#[default]` while the product docs describe the Auto preset as `workspace-write`; pin JevCode's default explicitly in defaults.ts and document it, do not rely on an implied default.
Codex `untrusted` approval policy is retired ("No longer supported; migration required"); do not copy older blog posts that still describe it.

[secondary, unverified] macOS seatbelt reportedly ignores `network_access = true` in Codex (openai/codex issue #10390); JevCode's seatbelt profile should be tested for network allow/deny explicitly rather than assumed.

Subagents that start fresh must re-gather context ("Latency matters. A subagent that isn't a fork starts fresh"), and every subagent "does its own model and tool work" (Codex), so parallelism raises cost and can raise wall time for small tasks.
Claude Code's concurrent-subagent error ("tells Claude not to retry") exists because generators retry limits; any lane cap in JevCode needs the same non-retryable wording in the outcome text.

Hooks: exit 2 blocks even if JSON says allow; `async: true` hooks have no enforced timeout; schema-invalid JSON is a non-blocking error that lets the action proceed. Design the hook contract with these three cases tested.

Background tasks: Claude Code kills them 5 s after a `-p` result, terminates at 5 GB output, and reaps under memory pressure after 30 idle minutes; a `-p` run with a background subagent stays open up to a 10-minute idle ceiling. Decide and document JevCode's equivalents before shipping `runBackground`.
Plan mode is not enforced in interactive terminals where bypassPermissions is available (Claude Code); enforce JevCode's plan gate in code for every runner so the guarantee does not depend on the UI.

Worktrees need at least one commit (`Failed to resolve base branch "HEAD"`); `-p` runs never clean up their worktrees; a killed session leaves a lock until the sweep; symlinked `.claude/worktrees` is refused; LFS files come as pointers because repo-local filter drivers are skipped. Handle all five in src/workspace/git.ts or the lane feature will strand checkouts.
A worktree is a fresh checkout: `.env` and other gitignored files are absent unless copied (`.worktreeinclude`), so a lane started without this cannot find its keys and would fall back to prompting.

Claude Code's classifier does not trust remotes added mid-session and presumes `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash drop` destroy work; a failed classifier call yields "cannot determine the safety" rather than allow. JevCode's hard-rule list must fail closed the same way when the Jev risk call times out.
Approval-reviewer models add cost ("This adds model usage" for Codex auto_review; classifier charges in Claude Code); Jev is already this reviewer, so do not layer a second LLM reviewer on top of it.
Codex GitHub docs/sandbox.md and docs/config.md are now one-line pointers to learn.chatgpt.com; cite the learn.chatgpt.com pages or codex-rs source, not the GitHub docs paths.

Codex `[agents]` thread default (6) and key names `max_threads`/`max_depth`/`job_max_runtime_seconds` come from third-party posts only; the official page names `max_concurrent_threads_per_session` without a default. Treat the number as unverified.

mechanisms.name: Client/server core with an in-process default transport and an SSE event bus
mechanisms.what: Every UI (TUI, desktop, web, IDE, ACP) is a client of one HTTP server (Hono). `opencode serve` listens on 127.0.0.1:4096 with OpenAPI at /doc; the TUI by default starts the server in a worker thread and talks to it over a fake URL (`http://opencode.internal`) so there is no socket hop; `opencode attach <url>` connects a terminal to a remote backend. All state changes are typed bus events streamed on `GET /event` (first event `server.connected`) and `GET /global/event`. Prompts can be fire-and-forget (`POST /session/:id/prompt_async` returns 204) and the TUI itself is drivable over `/tui/*` (submit-prompt, control/next, control/response). The SDK (`@opencode-ai/sdk`) exposes `createOpencode()` / `createOpencodeClient({baseUrl})`, `session.prompt/abort/share`, `event.subscribe()`, `tui.*`, structured output via `format: {type:'json_schema'}`.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Decouples the engine from any renderer: multiple clients, remote attach, scripting, IDE plugins and automated tests all reuse one API and one event stream; async prompt + events means the UI never blocks on the model. The in-process worker default keeps first-frame latency low while preserving the same API shape.
mechanisms.evidence: docs/server (fetched 2026-09-21): 'a headless HTTP server that exposes an OpenAPI endpoint that an opencode client can use'; default port 4096, hostname 127.0.0.1; `GET /event` 'First event is server.connected'; `POST /session/:id/prompt_async` returns '204 No Content'; `/tui/submit-prompt`, `/tui/control/next`, `/tui/control/response`; `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` basic auth. docs/sdk (2026-09-21): `createOpencode`, `createOpencodeClient({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:4096' })`, `event.subscribe()` 'Server-sent events stream', `session.prompt()` with `format: { type: 'json_schema' }`. docs/cli (2026-09-21): `opencode attach` 'Attach a terminal to an already running OpenCode backend server'. In-process worker/fake-URL transport and the 16 ms event coalescer are documented in the local note docs/research/tui/01-opencode.md §1 from R:packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts and R:packages/tui/src/context/sdk.tsx (fetched 2026-09-20).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode already has a typed engine->renderer event stream (src/core/events.ts, EngineEvent) and a session registry plan (docs/COORDINATION-DESIGN.md §3, §7 pause/resume from anywhere). Adopt the shape, not the stack: put the engine behind a tiny local RPC (in-process by default, optional loopback listener) whose events are the existing EngineEvents; make the Ink TUI, `jevcode sessions`, and the coordination watcher clients of it. This is what makes 'pause/resume/attach from another terminal' and a scriptable `run --format json` cheap. Jev is untouched: it stays a decider called by engine stages; nothing in the transport depends on Jev.

mechanisms.name: Primary agents vs subagents in child sessions, with foreground/background task tool, depth limit, task_id resume and derived permissions
mechanisms.what: Two agent kinds: primary (Build: all tools; Plan: edits denied, bash asks) cycled with Tab, and subagents (General, Explore; v1 docs also list Scout, v2 says 'V2 has no built-in scout agent') invoked by @mention or by the `task` tool. Each agent has `description`, `mode: primary|subagent|all`, `model` (provider/model), `prompt`, `temperature`/`top_p`, `steps`, `permission`, `hidden`, `color`; unknown keys pass through as provider options. Subagents run in child sessions with fresh context; they inherit the parent's model if none set. Source: `task` tool params `description`, `prompt`, `subagent_type`, `task_id` (resume a prior child session), `background` (gated by `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true`); nesting is capped by `subagent_depth` (default 1); the child's permission set = parent session's deny + external_directory rules, plus default denies for `todowrite` and `task` unless the subagent's own ruleset allows them; the parent is told 'DO NOT sleep, poll for progress, ask the task for status, or duplicate this task's work' and 'You will be notified automatically when it finishes'. Hidden `compaction`, `title`, `summary` agents do maintenance. Child sessions are navigable with keybinds session_child_first/cycle/parent.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Parallelism without context pollution: a subagent's exploration never lands in the parent's window, only its result does. Depth cap and derived deny-rules prevent runaway fan-out and privilege escalation; `task_id` lets a parent continue a specialist's session instead of restarting; background mode plus explicit 'do not poll' guidance stops the parent from wasting steps.

mechanisms.name: Nine-strategy fuzzy edit replacer chain with CRLF/BOM preservation, then diff + snapshot + LSP diagnostics + formatter in one tool call
mechanisms.what: The `edit` tool takes `oldString`/`newString`/`replaceAll`. `replace()` tries, in order: SimpleReplacer (exact), LineTrimmedReplacer, BlockAnchorReplacer (first/last line anchors, Levenshtein similarity >= 0.65 for middle lines), WhitespaceNormalizedReplacer, IndentationFlexibleReplacer, EscapeNormalizedReplacer, TrimmedBoundaryReplacer, ContextAwareReplacer, MultiOccurrenceReplacer; multiple matches throw 'Found multiple matches for oldString. Provide more surrounding context to make the match unique.' Line endings are normalised for matching and converted back to the file's ending; a BOM is preserved. After a successful write the tool builds a unified diff (`createTwoFilesPatch`), records a Snapshot.FileDiff, calls `lsp.touchFile(filePath, 'document')` and appends 'LSP errors detected in this file, please fix:' with the diagnostics block, and runs the formatter service. Header credits cline's diff-apply evals.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Most model edit failures are whitespace/indent/escape drift, not wrong intent. Recovering them in code saves a whole model round trip per failure and keeps the loop moving; folding diff, snapshot, diagnostics and formatting into the same tool result gives the model (or a judge) immediate, cheap feedback.

mechanisms.name: Shadow git-dir snapshots (objects/info/alternates + copied index) for per-turn undo/redo and diffs
mechanisms.what: Snapshots live in `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<projectId>/<hash(worktree)>` as a separate `--git-dir` pointed at the user's `--work-tree`. To avoid re-hashing, the shadow repo writes the user's repo object dirs into `objects/info/alternates` and seeds its index by copying the source `index`; it lists changed+untracked files with `diff-files -z` and `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`, drops newly-ignored paths, skips untracked files over 2 MiB (`limit = 2*1024*1024`), stages only allowed paths, and runs `gc --prune` periodically; operations are serialized with a per-gitdir lock. Interface: `track()`, `patch(hash)`, `restore(snapshot)`, `revert(patches)`, `diff(hash)`, `diffFull(from,to)`. `/undo` 'Removes the most recent user message, all subsequent responses, and any file changes'; `/redo` re-applies; 'your project needs to be a Git repository'. `snapshot: false` in config for large repos.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Whole-turn undo/redo and exact per-turn diffs without touching the user's index or creating commits, and without re-hashing a large tree (the source comment says a naive `git add --all` 'can take minutes' on chromium-sized checkouts). Untracked files are captured too, which plain `git stash`/HEAD-restore misses.

By doing this we eliminating this at all'; writes `objects/info/alternates`; 'Seed the index from the source repo so already-hashed entries are reused'; `const limit = 2 * 1024 * 1024`; `git(['init'], { env: { GIT_DIR: state.gitdir, GIT_WORK_TREE: state.worktree } })`; `lock(state.gitdir).withPermits(1)`. docs/tui (2026-09-21): '/undo: Undo last message in the conversation. Removes the most recent user message, all subsequent responses, and any file changes'; 'Internally, this uses Git to manage the file changes. So your project needs to be a Git repository.' docs/config (2026-09-21): 'OpenCode uses snapshots to track file changes during agent operations, enabling you to undo and revert changes'; disable 'for large repositories to improve indexing speed and reduce disk usage'.

Gives step-granular `/undo` and `/redo` in the TUI and a precise 'files touched this step' list for Jev's judge and for the coordination path leases (COORDINATION-DESIGN §4.3). Respect the existing sandbox rule that `.git/config`/hooks are write-denied for agent commands: the shadow gitdir is harness-owned, so it stays inside the run dir. Zero Jev involvement.

mechanisms.name: Three-stage context policy: prune old tool outputs, model-aware overflow check, then checkpoint-style compaction that restarts the turn
mechanisms.what: Stage 1 (prune, free): walking backwards, once 40,000 tokens (PRUNE_PROTECT) of tool output are protected, older tool outputs are erased if that frees more than 20,000 tokens (PRUNE_MINIMUM); `skill` outputs are never pruned. Stage 2 (overflow): `usable = input_limit ? input_limit - reserved : context - maxOutput`, where `reserved = compaction.reserved ?? min(20_000, maxOutputTokens)`; `isOverflow` when `tokens.total (or input+output+cache.read+cache.write) >= usable`, disabled by `compaction.auto: false` or `limit.context === 0`. Stage 3 (compaction): a hidden agent writes a checkpoint summary with required headings ('## Objective', decisions/completed/active work, blockers, next moves, relevant files); recent turns totalling 2,000-15,000 tokens (`keep.tokens`, default 15,000) are kept verbatim beside it, tool outputs in the serialized history are truncated to 2,000 chars, and the active user turn is cloned so the model restarts from the checkpoint. Native provider compaction is used when policy allows; `/compact` (alias `/summarize`) and `POST /session/:id/compact` trigger it manually and return before the summary is done. v1 keys were `prune`/`reserved`, v2 uses `auto`/`keep.tokens`/`buffer` (20,000).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Ordering matters for speed: pruning costs nothing and usually avoids a summary call; the overflow threshold derives from catalogue limits so it adapts per model; keeping a verbatim recent tail avoids the 'summary lost the exact error text' failure; restarting the turn from the checkpoint keeps the loop deterministic.
mechanisms.evidence: Source session/compaction.ts (2026-09-21): `export const PRUNE_MINIMUM = 20_000; export const PRUNE_PROTECT = 40_000; const TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS = 2_000; const PRUNE_PROTECTED_TOOLS = ['skill']; const MIN_PRESERVE_RECENT_TOKENS = 2_000; const MAX_PRESERVE_RECENT_TOKENS = 15_000`; comment 'goes backwards through parts until there are PRUNE_PROTECT tokens worth of tool calls, then erases output of older tool calls to free context space'; `if (pruned > PRUNE_MINIMUM)`. Source session/overflow.ts (2026-09-21): `const COMPACTION_BUFFER = 20_000`; `usable()` and `isOverflow()` as quoted; `if (input.cfg.compaction?.auto === false) return false`. v2 docs/compaction (2026-09-21): trigger 'estimated tokens >= min(input limit - buffer, context limit - max(output reserve, buffer))'; `keep.tokens` default 15000, `buffer` default 20000; summary 'must contain at least one requested heading such as ## Objective'; 'tool output (limited to 2,000 characters)'; manual compaction response 'confirms admission; it does not wait for the summary'. deepwiki 2.4 (secondary, 2026-09-21): 'Clones the active user interaction to restart the turn with cleaned context'; `ContextOverflowError` when even compaction cannot fit.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode has a fixed 4-step window (src/loop/window.ts: WINDOW_SIZE 4, WINDOW_OUTPUT_HEAD 400, TAIL 200) and COORDINATION-DESIGN §8 already plans tiered history, a context meter and `context.compaction: 'code'|'llm'|'off'` (default `code`). Concretely adopt: (a) `usable()` computed from the model catalogue's `limit.context/output` so the meter is model-aware; (b) 'code' compaction = opencode's prune (drop old tool outputs, protect the last N tokens and any Jev decision records); (c) 'llm' compaction = fixed-heading checkpoint using the `small_model` slot, not the generator; (d) keep a verbatim recent tail; (e) restart the step from the checkpoint. INFERENCE/proposal: Jev can Score which old outputs are safe to drop first, but thresholds and the trigger stay code so a Jev outage never blocks compaction.

The `read` tool defaults to 2,000 lines, caps lines at 2,000 chars ('... (line truncated to 2000 chars)'), refuses over 50 KB unless `offset`/`limit` are used, supports images (jpeg/png/gif/webp), suggests similar paths on a miss, lists directories, and forks `lsp.touchFile` in the background so diagnostics are warm without delaying the read.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Big outputs stop blowing the context while remaining fully recoverable via a path the model can `read` with offsets; bounded reads and line caps keep per-step tokens flat; background LSP warm-up hides server start latency.

mechanisms.name: Layered permissions: allow/ask/deny with glob and parsed-bash patterns, external_directory, doom_loop, once/always/reject UI
mechanisms.what: `permission` keys: read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task, external_directory, todowrite, webfetch, websearch, lsp, skill, question, doom_loop; each `allow|ask|deny` or a pattern map (e.g. `bash: {'git *': 'ask', 'grep *': 'allow'}`); bash patterns match the parsed command (web-tree-sitter grammars for bash and PowerShell, with cwd-changing commands `cd/pushd/...` tracked and `$HOME/$PWD` expansion) so `grep *` allows `grep pattern file.txt` while bare `grep` would not; file patterns use `*`/`?` with `~`/`$HOME` expansion; `external_directory` gates paths outside the worktree; `doom_loop` (default ask) fires when 'the same tool call repeats 3 times with identical input'. Agent rules override global ('Agent permissions are merged with the global config, and agent rules take precedence'); the prompt offers once / always (for the session) / reject. Tools are otherwise enabled by default; MCP tools are gated with `server_*` wildcards.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Most permission decisions become static pattern matches that never touch a model or a human; only the ambiguous middle reaches an interactive ask. Parsing (not regex) makes `bash` allow-lists safe against `a && rm -rf` tricks; doom_loop is a cheap circuit breaker.
mechanisms.evidence: docs/permissions (2026-09-21): three outcomes 'allow runs without approval, ask prompts for approval, and deny blocks the action'; '"grep *" allows grep pattern file.txt, while "grep" alone would block it'; '~/projects/* expands to /Users/username/projects/*'; 'Home expansion only affects how a pattern is written. It does not make an external path part of the current workspace'; doom_loop 'the same tool call repeats 3 times with identical input', default 'ask'; UI 'once... always... reject'. Source tool/shell.ts (2026-09-21): `import { Language, type Node } from 'web-tree-sitter'`, `const CWD = new Set(['cd','chdir','popd','pushd','push-location','set-location'])`, `import { BashArity } from '@/permission/arity'`. Secondary (shibuiwilliam gist, 2026-09-21): 'Session-level permissions (highest priority) -> Agent-level -> Global'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode routes every proposal through Jev's four risk Scores (destructive/out-of-scope/plan-mismatch/irreversible; >=0.7 blocks, 0.3-0.7 asks) and has signature-based loop detection (src/loop/loopdetect.ts, LOOP_TRIP_COUNT = 3). Add a code allow/deny pattern layer in front of the risk stage: allow-listed read-only commands (`grep *`, `ls *`, `git status`, `npm test`) skip the Jev risk call entirely; deny-listed patterns never reach Jev. That removes a Jev round trip from the commonest steps (Jev speeds things up, is not mission-critical) while keeping Jev for the ambiguous band. Use a real shell parser or the existing `sh -c` word-splitting with cwd tracking rather than regex. Keep JevCode's stronger signature-based loop detector; opencode's identical-input rule is a subset.

mechanisms.name: LSP as opt-in agent feedback: auto-spawn per extension, touch-and-wait for diagnostics, diagnostics appended to edit results; docs prefer CLI checks
mechanisms.what: `lsp` is disabled by default; when enabled (`lsp: true` or per-server `{command, extensions, env, initialization, disabled}`), opening/editing a file starts the matching server if not running (40+ definitions; some auto-install). `LSP.touchFile(path, 'document'|'full')` then `client.waitForDiagnostics({mode})`; `LSP.diagnostics()` aggregates per file; the edit tool appends 'LSP errors detected in this file, please fix:'; the experimental `lsp` tool exposes hover, definition, references, implementation, documentSymbol, workspaceSymbol, call hierarchy. The docs explicitly warn: 'Language servers can get out of sync, use significant memory, vary by version or project, and slow down agent workflows' and recommend running lint/typecheck CLIs documented in AGENTS.md/skills instead.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Compiler-grade feedback right after an edit is the highest-signal, lowest-token correction loop, but the maintainers' own guidance is that CLI diagnostics fed back into the loop are usually the better trade; the design shows the shape of the feedback (bounded block appended to the tool result) either way.
mechanisms.evidence: docs/lsp (2026-09-21): 'use diagnostics as feedback for the agent'; 'LSP is disabled by default'; quoted warning and 'In many projects it is better to have the agent run lint, typecheck, or other diagnostic CLI tools directly, so errors are fed back into the agent loop'. Source lsp/lsp.ts (2026-09-21): `touchFile: (input: string, diagnostics?: 'document' | 'full')`, `client.waitForDiagnostics({... mode: diagnostics})`, `spawning: Map<...>` dedupes concurrent spawns per root+server, functions `hover, definition, references, implementation, documentSymbol, workspaceSymbol, prepareCallHierarchy, incomingCalls, outgoingCalls`. Source tool/edit.ts lines 197-201 (quoted in the edit item). docs/tools: 'lsp (experimental) - Interact with your configured LSP servers to get code intelligence'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Do not add LSP servers (memory, startup latency, drift; conflicts with JevCode's <300 ms first frame and sandbox posture). INFERENCE/proposal: adopt the feedback shape with CLI checks JevCode already knows how to run in the sandbox: after each edit/write, run a project-detected fast check on the touched files (e.g. `tsc --noEmit -p` for TS, `ruff`/`pyright` for Python, detected like formatters are), append a bounded 'errors detected in this file, please fix' block to the ActionOutcome, and let Jev's judge Noul see it as a computed fact. Jev is not needed to produce the signal; it only benefits from it.

mechanisms.name: Automatic formatters after every write/edit, detected from project markers

mechanisms.name: Provider/model layer: models.dev catalogue with bundled snapshot, env-var credential resolution, provider/model ids, per-agent and small_model slots, variants, whitelist/blacklist, /connect, OpenAI-compatible recipe, curated Zen list

Credentials resolve env vars first (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, FIREWORKS_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, NVIDIA_API_KEY ...), then `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` written by `/connect` / `opencode auth login`, then config. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is added with `npm: '@ai-sdk/openai-compatible'`, `options.baseURL`, and a `models` map; `whitelist`/`blacklist` shrink the picker; `disabled_providers`/`enabled_providers` gate loading; `small_model` handles titles/summaries; `variants` (e.g. `{high: {reasoningEffort: 'high'}}`) cycle with ctrl+t; `/models` opens the picker; `opencode models --refresh` lists ids.
