mechanisms.name: Prompt caching as a first-class harness constraint (frozen prefix, breakpoint placement, pre-warm, hit-rate telemetry)
mechanisms.what: Structure every generator request as a byte-identical stable zone (tools sorted deterministically → system → early messages) followed by an active zone (plan, evidence, latest tool results), place cache_control on the last block whose prefix is identical across steps, never toggle request parameters that re-render the prompt between steps, delete from the tail (not the head) when trimming, pre-warm the cache at startup, and record cache read/write tokens per call so cache breaks are visible.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Anthropic docs (fetched 2026-09-21): cache reads bill at 0.1x base input (0.025x on Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1), 5-min writes 1.25x, 1-h writes 2.0x; prefix order is tools → system → messages and 'changes at each level invalidate that level and all subsequent levels'; up to 4 breakpoints, 20-block lookback; per-model minimum 512–4,096 tokens or the block is silently uncached; `tool_choice` changes invalidate the messages level; 'cache remains valid when only tool results are provided'; pre-warming with max_tokens: 0 'eliminates the cache-miss latency penalty on the first user interaction'. arXiv 2601.06007 (v2 2026-01-31, fetched 2026-09-21): 500+ agent sessions across OpenAI/Anthropic/Google, 41–80% cost reduction and 13–31% faster TTFT, but 'full-context caching ... can paradoxically increase latency'; exclude dynamic tool outputs and timestamps from cached blocks. yage.ai 2026-04-04 (fetched 2026-09-21): agent input:output ≈ 100:1, cache-unaware systems cost 3–5x more, 'every short-lived sub-agent means a cache cold start', delete history from the tail to preserve the prefix, sort tools deterministically. Datadog 2026-09-02 (fetched 2026-09-21): 69% of input tokens in March 2026 customer traces were system prompts; 'monitor cache hit rate rather than raw token consumption'.
mechanisms.evidence: Anthropic prompt-caching doc fetched 2026-09-21 (numbers above quoted verbatim). https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06007 fetched 2026-09-21 (41–80% cost, 13–31% TTFT, full-context caching can increase latency). https://yage.ai/share/prompt-caching-harness-constraint-en-20260404.html fetched 2026-09-21 (tail-delete rule, sub-agent cold starts, deterministic tool order, DeepSeek TTFT 13 s → 500 ms on 128K cache hit). https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/monitor-prompt-caching-optimize-token-usage/ fetched 2026-09-21 (69% system-prompt share).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Already partly done: src/provider/anthropic.ts marks system and the last tool with cache_control and parses cache_creation/cache_read tokens. Gaps [inference from code]: (1) `toolChoice` is rebuilt per step (auto / required / named tool) — per the Anthropic doc a tool_choice change invalidates the messages-level cache every time it flips, so keep it constant across steps or accept the miss deliberately; (2) the 4-step bounded window and the per-step plan-with-evidence rewrite the message body each step, so place the mutable plan/evidence AFTER the last breakpoint and keep the earlier steps' messages byte-stable (append-only); (3) sub-agents/lanes in docs/COORDINATION-DESIGN.md should share the exact same system+tools prefix to share the cache; (4) pre-warm the generator cache (max_tokens: 0) behind the ≤700 ms splash in jev-on mode; (5) surface cache-read ratio in generator.jsonl and the perf gates. Jev has no role here — this is pure code, off the mission-critical path, and it is the largest single latency/cost lever for jev-on. OpenRouter pass-through of cache_control for non-Anthropic generators is provider-dependent [unverified].

mechanisms.name: Speculative tool execution during model thinking time (PASTE-style pattern prefetch, read-only only)
mechanisms.what: Mine recurring tool-call sequences from the harness's own traces (e.g. edit → run tests, grep → read file), and while the generator is still streaming, speculatively execute the predicted next read-only tool on slack resources; promote the result if the authoritative call matches, discard otherwise; side-effecting tools only in dry-run.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: PASTE (arXiv 2603.18897, 2026-03-19, fetched 2026-09-21) reports 48.5% lower average task completion time, 1.8x tool throughput, 67% less tool-wait, 93.8% hit rate (any prediction matches) despite 27.8% top-1; on SWE-bench the 'Edit-Verify' pattern (55% of file edits followed by test execution) and 'Locate-Examine' (38% of grep followed by file access) drove the gains; 602 potentially side-effecting speculative actions out of 20,000+ were all prevented from committing. Speculative Interaction Agents (arXiv 2605.13360, 2026-05, fetched 2026-09-21): async I/O decoupling the reason-act thread plus speculative tool calling gives 1.3–1.7x on cloud models, 1.6–2.2x on 3B edge models.
mechanisms.evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.18897v1 fetched 2026-09-21 (48.5%, 1.8x, 93.8% hit rate, Edit-Verify 55%, Locate-Examine 38%, dry-run policy). https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13360 fetched 2026-09-21 (1.3–1.7x / 1.6–2.2x).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: [inference] JevCode's stage order is intent → context → propose → risk → execute → judge (src/loop/engine.ts). Jev's context Nouls name the relevant files before the generator proposes, so the harness can prefetch those files' bytes, stat and sha256 (the pre-image work in checkpoint/images.ts) during the propose stream, and can pre-run `git status`/`git diff` for the judge while the risk stage is deciding. After an `edit`/`write` executes, speculatively start the affected-tests run before the next step's intent/propose round trip when the mined pattern says a verify usually follows — tests are read-only w.r.t. the workspace (the sandbox already confines writes). Jev is the natural policy owner: its context decision is the speculation hint and a cheap Noul ('will the next action be a verify?') can gate whether to launch the speculative test run; a wrong guess only wastes slack CPU, so Jev stays off the mission-critical path. Never speculate edit/write/patch/run-with-side-effects.

mechanisms.name: Parallel tool calls and DAG execution for independent read-only actions
mechanisms.what: Let one model turn emit several independent tool calls (or batch several reads into one action), execute the independent read-only ones concurrently, run side-effecting ones sequentially, and return one tool_result per tool_use in a single user message.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: LLMCompiler (arXiv 2312.04511, fetched 2026-09-21): treating calls as a DAG gives up to 3.7x latency speedup, 6.7x cost reduction and ~9% accuracy gain over ReAct. Anthropic parallel-tool-use doc (fetched 2026-09-21): 'By default, Claude may call multiple tools in a single response ... Independent, read-only operations are usually safe to run in parallel for lower latency. Tools with side effects, shared state, or ordering requirements might be better run sequentially'; 'A run of consecutive tool_use blocks counts as one position' for the cache lookback, so parallel batches do not evict the cache. OpenDev (arXiv 2603.05344, 2026-03-05, fetched 2026-09-21) runs up to five read-only calls concurrently and writes sequentially. Anthropic multi-agent research post (2025-06-13, fetched 2026-09-21): parallel subagents plus parallel tool calls 'cut research time by up to 90% for complex queries' at ~15x token cost.
mechanisms.evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/parallel-tool-use fetched 2026-09-21. https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04511 fetched 2026-09-21 (3.7x, 6.7x, ~9%). https://arxiv.org/html/2603.05344v1 fetched 2026-09-21 (5 concurrent read-only calls). https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system fetched 2026-09-21 (up to 90% time reduction, 15x tokens).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: src/provider/anthropic.ts:109-112 hard-sets disable_parallel_tool_use: true because 'Jev owns control flow: exactly one action per step'. [inference] Keep one *decision* per step but allow a `read` action to carry several paths, or allow a parallel batch consisting only of read-class tools (read/grep/stat) to be treated as one step: the risk stage scores the batch once (reads are trivially low-risk), the executor runs them with Promise.all, and the judge sees one combined outcome. Investigate-heavy steps (which the intent Choice labels `investigate`) are where this pays; edit/run stay strictly single-action so Jev's safety gate is unchanged. For lanes/sub-agents (COORDINATION-DESIGN.md), the Anthropic result argues for breadth-parallel investigation with each lane returning a 1–2k-token summary, while the 15x token cost argues for Jev gating how many lanes to spawn.

mechanisms.name: Streaming edits and speculative/predicted-output apply (fine-grained tool streaming, speculative edits, predicted outputs)
mechanisms.what: Stream tool-call parameters without server-side buffering so the harness can start validating/applying an edit while the model is still generating; for whole-file rewrites, hand the server the original file as the draft so unchanged spans are accepted in bulk (speculative edits / predicted outputs).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Anthropic fine-grained tool streaming doc (fetched 2026-09-21): setting `eager_input_streaming: true` on a tool 'delivers a tool's input to your client as Claude generates it, without server-side buffering or JSON validation', reducing 'time to the first fragment of a large parameter, such as ... a block of code'; the client may receive partial/invalid JSON and must guard the parse and return `{"INVALID_JSON": ...}` with is_error. Cursor instant-apply post (2024-05-14, fetched 2026-09-21): speculative edits use the existing file as the draft, ~1,000 tokens/s (~3,500 chars/s) on a 70B model, ~13x over vanilla Llama-3-70B and ~9x over their prior GPT-4 deployment; planning (frontier model) and applying (fast model) are split. Fireworks (2024-06-23, fetched 2026-09-21): the client supplies the prediction, the server matches the longest prefix at temperature 0. OpenAI Predicted Outputs doc (fetched 2026-09-21): targets 'regenerating a text or code file with minor modifications'; rejected prediction tokens are billed; not supported with `tools`, n>1, logprobs, max_completion_tokens. EfficientEdit (arXiv 2506.02780, fetched 2026-09-21): edit-oriented speculative decoding up to 10.38x/13.09x over autoregressive decoding on CanItEdit/CodeIF-Bench.
mechanisms.evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/fine-grained-tool-streaming fetched 2026-09-21. https://cursor.com/blog/instant-apply fetched 2026-09-21 (1000 tok/s, 13x, 9x). https://fireworks.ai/blog/cursor fetched 2026-09-21. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/predicted-outputs fetched 2026-09-21 (no tools, rejected tokens billed). https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02780 fetched 2026-09-21 (10.38x/13.09x).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Already: anthropic.ts:95 sets eager_input_streaming: true and streams tool JSON. [inference] Exploit it: the `edit` tool is exact-match unique old/new — begin the unique-match search for `old` the moment that field closes in the stream, and if it definitely does not match (or matches more than once) abort the stream and re-prompt immediately instead of paying for the full `new` body plus a wasted risk/execute/judge round; pre-compute the target file's pre-image hash while `new` streams. For `write` of whole files on OpenAI-compatible providers, predicted outputs is unusable with tool calling, so only a fenced-JSON/no-tools fallback could use it — low priority. Jev has no role in the apply path (pure code).

mechanisms.name: Incremental structural repo index / ranked repo map for context selection
mechanisms.what: Maintain a cheap symbol/definition index (tree-sitter tags, LSP symbols, or a compiler-API graph) updated incrementally from changed files, and use a ranked, token-budgeted map (PageRank over the def/ref graph) or symbol-level tools instead of whole-file reads and repeated grep.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Aider repomap (2023-10-22, fetched 2026-09-21): tree-sitter def/ref tags, graph ranking, default `--map-tokens` 1,000, shows signatures rather than bodies. Serena (github.com/oraios/serena, fetched 2026-09-21): LSP-backed find_symbol / find_referencing_symbols / get_symbols_overview / replace_symbol_body over 40+ languages, claimed to collapse '8–12 careful, error-prone steps into one atomic call'. cocoindex realtime-codebase-indexing (fetched 2026-09-21): tree-sitter chunking, only changed chunks re-embedded, live watch mode. arXiv 2606.22417 'Code Isn't Memory' (2026-06-21, fetched 2026-09-21): structural index gives 'large localization gain', 'lower cost per solve' and is 'cheaper to run ... than agentic grep' on SWE-PolyBench Verified / SWE-bench Pro with Opus 4.7; benefits concentrate 'in multi-file changes'. arXiv 2604.18413 (2026-04-21, fetched 2026-09-21): compiler-API indexing beat tree-sitter+LSP RPC for TypeScript but full builds took 35 s (147K LOC) to 705 s (1.23M LOC) — so the index must be built once and updated incrementally, never on the request path.
mechanisms.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22417 fetched 2026-09-21. https://aider.chat/2023/10/22/repomap.html fetched 2026-09-21. https://github.com/oraios/serena fetched 2026-09-21. https://github.com/cocoindex-io/realtime-codebase-indexing fetched 2026-09-21. https://arxiv.org/html/2604.18413v2 fetched 2026-09-21 (35.2 s / 239.9 s / 705.6 s build times).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: src/workspace/candidates.ts already caches a path listing and re-lists only after a `run`; Jev's context Nouls choose among path-keyed candidates. [inference] Add a per-file def index (function/class names, import edges) built once at session open and patched from `changedFiles` after each edit; feed Jev richer per-candidate features (defs matching task keywords, import-distance to already-touched files) so the context stage needs fewer candidates and fewer read steps. Honor the zero-runtime-dependency rule: tree-sitter WASM would have to be inlined into dist/jevcode.mjs or replaced by `git grep -n` def-pattern extraction (Python `def`/`class`, TS `function`/`class`/`export`), which is fast enough for the flat-tokens-per-step goal. Keep it advisory: if the index is missing or stale, fall back to the current path-only candidates — Jev still decides, code still gates.

mechanisms.name: Test impact analysis: run affected tests first, full suite only at the completion gate
mechanisms.what: Map changed files to the tests that reach them (static import/call graph, or recorded runtime coverage) and run only that subset after each edit; reserve the full suite for the final done gate.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: TDAD (arXiv 2603.17973, 2026-03-19, fetched 2026-09-21): a code–test dependency graph (File/Function/Class/Test nodes; CONTAINS/CALLS/IMPORTS/TESTS/INHERITS edges) exposed as a grep-able test_map.txt cut regressions 6.08% → 1.82% (−70%) and pass-to-pass failures 562 → 155 with Qwen3-Coder 30B, and +8pp resolution in phase 2; notably TDD instructions WITHOUT the graph worsened regressions to 9.94%. pytest-testmon (github, fetched 2026-09-21): `--testmon` builds a .testmondata dependency DB on first run and afterwards 'selects and re-executes only tests affected by recent changes'; limitations: non-Python dependencies, dynamic imports, external files. testpick article (2024-06-18, fetched 2026-09-21): `vitest --changed` and `jest --findRelatedTests` walk the static import graph and miss data-driven module loading; recording per-test runtime coverage fixes it.
mechanisms.evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17973 fetched 2026-09-21 (6.08% → 1.82%, 562 → 155, 9.94% without graph). https://github.com/tarpas/pytest-testmon fetched 2026-09-21. https://dev.to/kazutaka-dev/why-vitest-changed-misses-some-tests-and-how-runtime-coverage-fixes-it-jjm fetched 2026-09-21.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: src/workspace/tests.ts already detects the runner (pytest/unittest/Django runtests/npm/cargo/go) and exposes a ScopeBuilder(targets) → command, and the judge consumes code-parsed test counts. [inference] After an edit/write/patch, build the affected set from the def/import index (mechanism 5) or the runner's own selector (`pytest --testmon`, `vitest related <files>`, `jest --findRelatedTests <files>`) and run that as the default verify; code enforces one full run before `done` is accepted (the completion Noul only sees full-suite counts). Jev's fit: a `scope` Choice per verify step — `affected | full` — with hard code rules (full when the affected set is empty/unknown, after N consecutive affected-only passes, and before finish). This is where most wall-clock goes on real repos, and the fallback keeps correctness in code.

mechanisms.name: Warm execution environment: snapshot/restore sandboxes, persistent shells, copy-on-write checkpoints
mechanisms.what: Avoid paying process/VM/interpreter cold start on every action: restore sandboxes from warm snapshots, keep a persistent shell or test-runner process alive between commands, and take checkpoints as copy-on-write clones instead of byte copies.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: bex.co on E2B/Firecracker (2026-07-31, fetched 2026-09-21): Firecracker cold boot ~125 ms vs snapshot-restore from a pre-warmed pool 5–30 ms best case, and 'the remaining milliseconds and the real engineering effort actually go' into pooling/image resolution/scheduling. DeltaBox (arXiv 2605.22781, 2026-05/06, fetched 2026-09-21): layered CoW filesystem + fork-from-frozen-template gives 14 ms checkpoint and 5 ms rollback, because 'subsequent checkpoints in AI agents are highly similar'. Engine Labs Terminal Bench post (2025-07, fetched 2026-09-21): switching from per-command child_process to a persistent node-pty session fixed REPL/long-running cases, but command completion had to be detected by output-stability heuristics ('almost like we're asking if we can solve the halting problem'). APFS folder clones (mjtsai 2026-05-14, fetched 2026-09-21): clonefile(2) is instantaneous CoW, `cp -c` clones per file, but Apple says 'the use of clonefile(2) to clone directory hierarchies is strongly discouraged'.
mechanisms.evidence: https://bex.co/blog/2026/07/31/e2b-sandbox-growth-firecracker-self-hosted-agent-sandbox fetched 2026-09-21 (125 ms vs 5–30 ms). https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22781 fetched 2026-09-21 (14 ms / 5 ms). https://enginelabs.substack.com/p/engine-labs-achieves-leading-terminal fetched 2026-09-21. https://mjtsai.com/blog/2026/05/14/apfs-folder-clones/ fetched 2026-09-21.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: src/sandbox/run.ts:270 spawns a fresh detached `sh -c` per action under sandbox-exec, so every verify re-pays shell + interpreter + test-collection startup. [inference, low-risk subset] (1) Replace the pre-image byte copy in checkpoint/images (16 MiB/step hash budget) with per-file `cp -c` clones on APFS (instant, CoW; do NOT clonefile directories) and hash lazily off the step path; (2) keep the runner warm where the runner supports it (pytest `--testmon`/cache dir kept between steps, vitest `--changed`), which is a warm cache rather than a persistent process and so preserves the existing tree-kill/output-cap/timeout semantics; (3) a true persistent shell is a bigger change: it conflicts with the per-command process-group kill and the 'when is it done' detection, so gate it behind a mode and keep per-command spawn as default. No Jev involvement; pure code.

mechanisms.name: Small router/decider before the expensive rollout (Jev's slot: tier routing, early abstention, escalation)
mechanisms.what: Use a small, calibrated model to decide — before spending frontier-model tokens — which generator tier or path a step needs, when to abstain/escalate, and when a cheap attempt should be abandoned; the harness enforces ceilings and forced escalation so routing errors are bounded.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Applied Compute (2026-06-04, fetched 2026-09-21): a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B router trained with GRPO (binary reward) 'to make a decision before the expensive model rollout begins', seeing the issue plus read-only repo context, hit ~76% on held-out SWE-bench Verified at ~25% lower cost than always-Opus 4.7 while matching GPT-5.5; 'small specialized routers outperformed frontier models at the routing task itself'. Agent-as-a-Router (arXiv 2606.22902, 2026-06, fetched 2026-09-21): execution-grounded experience (Orchestrator/Verifier/Memory statistics) alone gave a 15.3% relative gain over baseline routers across ~10,000 tasks and 8 models. Cost-Saving Cascades with Early Abstention (arXiv 2502.09054, 2025-03, fetched 2026-09-21): letting cheap models abstain early cut cost 13.0% and error 5.0% for +4.1% abstention because 'error patterns of small and large models are correlated'. Unblocked (2026-06-09, fetched 2026-09-21): routing saves 30–40% on simple tasks but the 'almost right' trap (cheap output that compiles but is wrong) can make rework exceed frontier cost; routers need context, not just the task text; token use on identical tasks varied up to 30x.
mechanisms.evidence: https://www.appliedcompute.com/research/training-an-agentic-router fetched 2026-09-21 (~76% pass, ~25% cheaper, decides before rollout). https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22902 fetched 2026-09-21 (15.3% relative gain). https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09054 fetched 2026-09-21 (13.0% cost, 5.0% error). https://getunblocked.com/blog/model-routing-coding-agents/ fetched 2026-09-21 (almost-right trap, 30x variance).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: This is exactly where a calibrated decider like Jev fits without being mission-critical. [inference] (1) Per-step tier Choice (`cheap | strong` generator, e.g. GLM 5.3 Flash vs Sonnet 5 via the same Provider interface) fed with structured signals — intent, number of candidate files, cross-file span, recent judge failures, error class — not just the task text (Unblocked's warning); code owns the ceilings: force `strong` after N failed cheap edits, never route the risk gate. (2) In jev-only mode, Jev already decides whether code-proposed candidate fixes suffice; extend with an explicit 'abstain → escalate to LLM' Noul so cheap synth attempts stop early instead of exhausting the budget. (3) Record routing outcomes in decisions.jsonl and fold them back as Agent-as-a-Router-style per-repo statistics for the next session. Wrong routes cost time, not safety: execution is still gated by the risk stage and verified by tests.

mechanisms.name: Early stopping on verifiers and confidence (first-verified-wins lanes, confidence-gated termination, replay instead of resample)
mechanisms.what: When several candidate fixes or trajectories run, stop everything as soon as one passes the verifier; terminate low-confidence generations mid-stream; and when retrying, branch from a good prefix of an earlier trajectory instead of starting over.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: DeepConf (arXiv 2508.15260, 2025-08-21, fetched 2026-09-21): online early termination on sliding-window group confidence (16-trace warm-up, threshold at top-10%/90%) cut tokens 43–84.7% (DeepConf-low) or 18–59% (DeepConf-high) with equal or better accuracy, no training, integrable in vLLM. CodeMonkeys (arXiv 2501.14723, 2025-01, fetched 2026-09-21): parallel trajectories that generate a test script alongside each edit, selected by model-generated-test voting plus a selection trajectory, 57.4% SWE-bench Verified for ~$2,300 — parallel sampling amortizes context scanning. R2E-Gym (arXiv 2504.07164, 2025-04, fetched 2026-09-21): execution-based and execution-free verifiers each plateau at 42–43% but combined reach 51% with a 32B open model. SWE-Replay (arXiv 2601.22129, 2026-02, fetched 2026-09-21): branching from intermediate steps of archived trajectories gives up to 17.4% cost reduction while maintaining or improving pass rate by up to 3.8%. interwhen (arXiv 2602.11202, 2026-02/05, fetched 2026-09-21): periodic test-time verification that forks inference and intervenes mid-trace reached near-perfect accuracy 'using a fraction of the tokens of baselines' and raised Qwen3-30B agentic completion 32% → 87%.
mechanisms.evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15260 fetched 2026-09-21 (43–84.7% / 18–59% token savings). https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14723 fetched 2026-09-21 (57.4%, ~$2,300). https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07164 fetched 2026-09-21 (51%). https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22129 fetched 2026-09-21 (up to 17.4% cost, +3.8%). https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11202 fetched 2026-09-21.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: jev-only already has parallel lanes (src/synth/llm/repro.ts runs candidates on lanes with Promise.all) and a completion Noul with a 0.85 stop threshold. [inference] (1) Make lanes first-verified-wins: as soon as one candidate passes the affected tests and the judge Nouls clear, abort the other lanes' processes (the sandbox tree-kill exists) — this converts parallelism into wall-clock savings. (2) Use Jev's client-computed confidence as a DeepConf-style gate for redundant work only: skip a second confirmation round trip or a re-plan when confidence is high, but never skip the risk stage. (3) On stream: abort the generator early when the harness can already prove the proposal invalid (mechanism 4). (4) On replan after loop detection, resume from the checkpointed pre-loop step (SWE-Replay's branch-from-prefix) rather than re-investigating from scratch — checkpoints per step already exist. Jev decides which lane/prefix to keep; tests remain the verifier of record.

mechanisms.name: Context condensation and tool-result clearing (bounded, linear-cost context)
mechanisms.what: Keep only recent tool interactions verbatim, replace older tool results with pointers or short summaries, and compact rarely and from the tail so the cached prefix survives; prefer clearing over LLM summarization when no extra call is needed.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: OpenHands condenser blog (2025-04-09, fetched 2026-09-21): condensation bounds per-turn cost to 'less than half' of baseline (up to 2x cost reduction) with 54% vs 53% resolution — baseline cost grows quadratically, condensed grows linearly; SDK docs (fetched 2026-09-21): trigger at max_size 120 events, keep_first 4, compress to ~60. Anthropic context-engineering post (2025-09-29, fetched 2026-09-21): pursue 'the smallest set of high-signal tokens'; Claude Code compaction keeps architectural decisions, unresolved bugs and the five most recently accessed files and discards raw tool outputs; tool-result clearing is 'one of the safest lightest touch forms of compaction'; sub-agents return 1,000–2,000-token summaries. 'Less Context, Better Agents' (arXiv 2606.10209, 2026-06-08, fetched 2026-09-21): pruning to the last 5 tool pairs plus a summary cut runtime 14.56 h → 5.79 h and tokens 1.48M → 0.55M while raising completion 71.0% → 91.6%. OpenDev (arXiv 2603.05344, fetched 2026-09-21): per-tool-type summarization, large-output offload to files, 'agent-aware truncation hints'.
mechanisms.evidence: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents fetched 2026-09-21. https://www.openhands.dev/blog/openhands-context-condensensation-for-more-efficient-ai-agents fetched 2026-09-21 (≤2x cost, 54% vs 53%). https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk/arch/condenser fetched 2026-09-21 (120 / 4 / ~60). https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10209 fetched 2026-09-21 (14.56 h → 5.79 h; 71.0% → 91.6%). https://arxiv.org/html/2603.05344v1 fetched 2026-09-21.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Already strong: the persistent plan-with-evidence plus a bounded 4-step window keeps ~12k generator tokens per step flat from step 1 to step 25 (docs/STATUS.md), and outputs are capped at 200 KB with a 16 KB summary tail. [inference] Remaining wins: replace older steps' raw tool outputs inside the window with one-line pointers to steps.jsonl/transcript.log (clearing, no extra LLM call), and structure the window so that dropping a step removes a block at the END of the stable prefix rather than rewriting earlier blocks (mechanism 1). Jev already picks which evidence lines the plan keeps (0.7/0.3 bands) — that is the right decider role; do not add an LLM summarizer on the step path.

mechanisms.name: Fast pre-verifiers before the test suite (shadow-workspace lints, syntax/type checks as judge facts)
mechanisms.what: After an edit and before the (slow) test run, execute cheap deterministic checks — syntax compile, linter, incremental type check, language-server diagnostics on the shadow copy — and feed the result to the judge so obviously broken edits are fixed without paying for a test run.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Cursor shadow workspace (2024-09-01, fetched 2026-09-21): a hidden workspace lets the AI see LSP lints for its own edits; 'Lints allow going from 90% working code to 100% working code'; initial language-server startup is slow and subsequent requests are fast; rust-analyzer needs files on disk. OpenDev (arXiv 2603.05344, fetched 2026-09-21) similarly separates read-only plan mode and adds self-critique before execution. R2E-Gym (arXiv 2504.07164, fetched 2026-09-21) shows execution-free verifiers are complementary to execution-based ones.
mechanisms.evidence: https://cursor.com/blog/shadow-workspace fetched 2026-09-21 ('90% to 100%', LS startup cost, rust-analyzer caveat). https://arxiv.org/html/2603.05344v1 fetched 2026-09-21. https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07164 fetched 2026-09-21.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: [inference] After edit/write/patch, run `python -m py_compile <file>` / `ruff check <file>` / `tsc --noEmit --incremental` / `cargo check` when the tool exists in the workspace (never install anything), in the same sandbox, with a short timeout, and pass `syntaxOk`/`diagnosticsCount` as code-computed facts into the judge criteria alongside test counts — the judge Nouls then decide 'fix first' vs 'run tests'. The check is a few hundred ms versus a multi-second test run, and a failure short-circuits a whole step. Jev decides what to do with the signal; code computes it; a missing tool just means the fact is absent.

mechanisms.name: Overlap harness work with model latency (asynchronous stage pipeline, eager construction, warm-up during splash)
mechanisms.what: Treat the loop as a pipeline: build prompts and tool schemas once at startup, overlap checkpoint writes, candidate refresh and state assembly with in-flight model/decider requests, and warm caches during idle UI time so no step waits on harness bookkeeping.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Speculative Interaction Agents (arXiv 2605.13360, fetched 2026-09-21): decoupling the reason-act thread from waiting on environment I/O gives 1.3–1.7x on cloud models. OpenDev (arXiv 2603.05344, fetched 2026-09-21): 'eager agent construction' of system prompts and tool schemas at init 'eliminating first-call latency', plus provider-level caching of a modular system prompt. Anthropic prompt-caching doc (fetched 2026-09-21): pre-warm with max_tokens: 0 so the first real request hits the cache. Anthropic multi-agent post (2025-06-13, fetched 2026-09-21): subagents currently run synchronously; asynchronous execution is named as the next latency win.
mechanisms.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13360 fetched 2026-09-21. https://arxiv.org/html/2603.05344v1 fetched 2026-09-21. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching fetched 2026-09-21 (pre-warm). https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system fetched 2026-09-21.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Already: the candidate cache refresh and plan serialisation overlap the intent request, and step N's checkpoint write overlaps step N+1 up to the execute stage (docs/DESIGN.md); the launcher enables the Node compile cache and renders the splash before any network. [inference] Extend: (1) assemble the risk-stage Jev state while the proposal streams and fire the Jev request the instant the tool call closes (Jev round trips are ~170 ms each, 3–4 per step per DESIGN.md — saving one serialization hop per step is real but small); (2) reuse a Jev answer within a step when the request hash (src/jev/client.ts:436) is unchanged; (3) use the ≤700 ms splash to open the HTTPS connections to the Jev and generator hosts and pre-warm the generator cache in jev-on. All code; Jev untouched.

speed_tricks: Freeze the prefix: identical system text and deterministically ordered tool definitions every step; put the mutable plan/evidence and latest tool results AFTER the last cache_control breakpoint; make the message history append-only inside the 4-step window (drop from the tail, never rewrite earlier blocks). (Anthropic prompt-caching doc; yage.ai 2026-04-04; both fetched 2026-09-21)

Stop flipping tool_choice between steps in src/provider/anthropic.ts (auto/required/named) unless the miss is intended — a tool_choice change invalidates the messages-level cache. (Anthropic doc, fetched 2026-09-21)

Pre-warm the generator cache with a max_tokens: 0 request and open the Jev/generator HTTPS connections behind the ≤700 ms splash, so step 1 is a cache read. (Anthropic doc, fetched 2026-09-21) [inference on splash placement]

Log cache_read/cache_creation ratio per call (fields already parsed) into generator.jsonl and add a perf row 'cache read share ≥ X%' so cache breaks are caught by the existing gates. (Datadog 2026-09-02, fetched 2026-09-21)

Speculate reads only: when Jev's context Nouls name files, prefetch bytes/stat/sha256 during the propose stream; pre-run git status/diff for the judge; after an edit, speculatively start the affected-tests run when the mined Edit→Verify pattern predicts it (PASTE: 55% of edits are followed by tests). Never speculate edit/write/patch or side-effecting run. (arXiv 2603.18897, fetched 2026-09-21)

Stream-validate edits: start the unique exact-match search for `old` as soon as that field closes in the eager_input_streaming stream; abort the generation and re-prompt on a definite mismatch instead of paying for `new` plus a wasted risk/execute/judge round. [inference on top of the Anthropic fine-grained streaming doc, fetched 2026-09-21]

Allow a read-class batch (several read/grep paths) as one step: one risk score, Promise.all execution, one judge outcome; keep edit/run strictly single-action so Jev's gate is unchanged. (Anthropic parallel-tool-use doc; LLMCompiler 3.7x; both fetched 2026-09-21) [inference]

Affected tests first, full suite only before `done`: use the runner's own selector (pytest --testmon, vitest related/--changed, jest --findRelatedTests) or the def/import index through the existing ScopeBuilder; code forces a full run when the affected set is unknown/empty and before finish. (TDAD arXiv 2603.17973; testmon; testpick article; all fetched 2026-09-21)

Cheap pre-verifiers as judge facts: py_compile/ruff/tsc --noEmit --incremental/cargo check on touched files (only if already installed) before any test run; a failure short-circuits the step. (Cursor shadow workspace 2024-09-01, fetched 2026-09-21) [inference]

Instant checkpoints: per-file `cp -c` (APFS clonefile) for pre-images instead of read+hash on the step path; hash lazily; never clonefile a directory (Apple: strongly discouraged). (mjtsai 2026-05-14, fetched 2026-09-21)

Keep runner caches warm between steps (pytest cache/.testmondata, vitest cache dir) rather than a persistent shell, so the per-command process-group kill, output cap and timeout semantics stay intact. (Engine Labs 2025-07 on persistent-session completion-detection pain, fetched 2026-09-21)

Jev as tier router: a per-step `cheap | strong` generator Choice fed with structured signals (intent, candidate count, cross-file span, recent judge failures, error class), with code-owned ceilings: force `strong` after N failed cheap edits; never route the risk gate. (Applied Compute 2026-06-04; Unblocked 2026-06-09; both fetched 2026-09-21)

First-verified-wins lanes in jev-only: abort sibling lanes the moment one candidate passes affected tests and the judge Nouls clear; on replan, branch from the checkpointed pre-loop step instead of re-investigating. (CodeMonkeys; SWE-Replay up to 17.4% cost; both fetched 2026-09-21) [inference]

Reuse Jev answers within a step when the request hash is unchanged, and fire the risk request the instant the tool call closes with state assembled during streaming (3–4 Jev round trips × ~170 ms per step per DESIGN.md). [inference]

Clear, don't summarize: inside the 4-step window replace older raw tool outputs with one-line pointers to steps.jsonl/transcript.log; no extra LLM call on the step path. (Anthropic context-engineering 2025-09-29; arXiv 2606.10209 14.56 h → 5.79 h; both fetched 2026-09-21)

Measure what you speed up: per-step harnessMs (already gated < 50 ms p95), speculative hit rate, tests-run/tests-total, cache read share, and Jev round trips per step — iterate on small tasks, not full benchmarks.
pitfalls: Full-context caching can INCREASE latency; cache only the stable zone and keep dynamic tool results/timestamps out of cached blocks. (arXiv 2601.06007, fetched 2026-09-21)

Silent non-caching below the per-model minimum (512–4,096 tokens depending on model) — a short system prompt marked cache_control is simply not cached and no error is returned; the 5-min TTL counts from request start, so a long generation eats into the reuse window. (Anthropic doc, fetched 2026-09-21)

Any change to tools invalidates everything; tool_choice, images, thinking/effort/speed settings invalidate downstream levels; nondeterministic tool ordering or head-side history deletion destroys the prefix. (Anthropic doc; yage.ai; fetched 2026-09-21)

Sub-agents/lanes each start with a cold cache; share the exact same system+tools prefix or the 15x token cost of parallel agents gets worse. (yage.ai 2026-04-04; Anthropic multi-agent post; fetched 2026-09-21)

Speculation must never commit side effects: PASTE caught 602 potentially side-effecting speculative actions in 20,000+; speculated results must be matched to the authoritative call (hash/args) before promotion and preempted under contention. (arXiv 2603.18897, fetched 2026-09-21)

Parallel tool calls: side-effecting, shared-state or order-dependent tools must run sequentially; return a tool_result for every tool_use (is_error for skipped ones) or the next turn is malformed. (Anthropic parallel-tool-use doc, fetched 2026-09-21)

Fine-grained tool streaming delivers partial/invalid JSON; guard the parse, handle max_tokens cut-offs mid-parameter, and return {"INVALID_JSON": ...} with is_error — a naive early-apply on partial input corrupts files. (Anthropic doc, fetched 2026-09-21)

Test selection misses dynamic imports, registries, non-code assets and config changes (static import graphs; testmon's stated limits) — always run the full suite before `done`; TDAD found procedure without the dependency graph WORSENED regressions to 9.94%. (testpick article; testmon README; arXiv 2603.17973; fetched 2026-09-21)

Router 'almost right' trap: cheap-model retries can exceed the frontier model's one-shot cost; routers misroute when given thin context; token use on identical tasks varies up to 30x, so budget by ceilings not averages. (Unblocked 2026-06-09, fetched 2026-09-21)
Confidence-based early stopping needs calibration (DeepConf uses a 16-trace warm-up); Jev's client-computed confidence should gate only redundant work, never the risk stage or the final verification.

Persistent shells make 'is the command finished' a heuristic (output-stability windows fail on quiet long builds) and break per-command process-group kill/output-cap semantics; JevCode's sandbox assumes one process tree per action. (Engine Labs 2025-07, fetched 2026-09-21)
APFS: clonefile(2) on directory hierarchies is 'strongly discouraged' by Apple (kernel stall/panic risk); clone per file with cp -c. (mjtsai 2026-05-14, fetched 2026-09-21)

Repo indexes are expensive to build (35 s to 705 s for TS compiler-API indexing of 147K–1.23M LOC) and go stale after edits — build once, update incrementally from changedFiles, and never block a step on it; JevCode's zero-runtime-dependency rule excludes tree-sitter WASM unless inlined. (arXiv 2604.18413, fetched 2026-09-21)

Condensation/compaction rewrites history and therefore breaks the cache prefix; do it rarely and at the tail; OpenHands' resolution gain from condensation was only +1pp (54% vs 53%) — it is a cost/latency lever, not a quality lever. (openhands.dev 2025-04-09; yage.ai; fetched 2026-09-21)

OpenAI Predicted Outputs cannot be combined with tool calls and bills rejected prediction tokens — incompatible with JevCode's tool-call edit format except in a no-tools fallback. (OpenAI doc, fetched 2026-09-21)

Shadow-workspace style LSP pre-verification has a slow first start and some servers (rust-analyzer) need files on disk; treat diagnostics as optional facts, not a gate. (Cursor 2024-09-01, fetched 2026-09-21)

Do not let speed work move Jev onto mission-critical paths: every mechanism above keeps execution gating (risk stage), test verification and budgets in code; Jev only chooses among safe alternatives (which files to prefetch, which tier, which scope, which lane to keep).
