mechanisms.name: Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) principles with measured ablations (SWE-agent)
mechanisms.what: Purpose-built agent tools obeying four rules: actions simple and easy to understand; actions compact (navigation/editing consolidated into few commands); feedback informative but concise; guardrails that stop error propagation (lint gate on edits, file viewer windows, summarised search, empty-output message). The paper ablates each on SWE-bench Lite.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Interface design alone moved SWE-bench Lite from 12.7-15.7% to 18.0% with the same model. The concrete numbers tell you which knobs matter: lint-gated edits +3.0pp, summarised search vs iterative search +6.0pp, a 100-line viewer window vs full file +5.3pp, last-5-observation context vs full history +3.0pp.
mechanisms.evidence: arXiv 2405.15793 (HTML, fetched 2026-09-21), ablation table on SWE-bench Lite: Edit with linting 18.0% vs without 15.0%; Search summarized 18.0% / iterative 12.0% / none 15.7%; File viewer 100 lines 18.0% / 30 lines 14.3% / full file 12.7%; Context last 5 observations 18.0% / full history 15.0% / without demo 16.3%. Principles quoted: 'Actions should be simple and easy to understand', 'Actions should be compact and efficient', 'Environment feedback should be informative but concise', 'Guardrails mitigate error propagation and hasten recovery'. swe-agent.com/latest/background/aci/ (fetched 2026-09-21): 'We add a linter that runs when an edit command is issued, and do not let the edit command go through if the code isn't syntactically correct'; viewer shows 'just 100 lines in each turn'; search 'simply list[s] each file that had at least one match. Showing the model more context about each match proved to be too confusing for the model'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Directly shapes JevCode's six-action applier (edit/write/patch/run/read/done, DESIGN.md §0.2). Adopt as code rules, not Jev questions: (1) a syntax-check gate after `edit`/`write`/`patch` before the step commits (py_compile / `node --check` by extension) with the SWE-agent verbatim error strings the repo already copies; (2) `read` returns a 100-line window with a `line` argument rather than whole files; (3) `localize`/`search` results return the matching file list first, match lines only on request. Jev's context Nouls (stages/context.ts) then pick from a short list, which is cheaper and faster. None of this touches a mission-critical path; it removes tokens per step.

mechanisms.name: Structured per-turn state and explicit empty-output feedback (SWE-agent state_command, diff_state, next_step_no_output_template)
mechanisms.what: After every action a state executable emits JSON (open_file, working_dir, optionally the current git diff) that is templated into the next prompt; when a command prints nothing the harness says so explicitly instead of returning a blank observation.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: The model never has to guess where it is or whether a silent command worked; the diff-in-state keeps the accumulated change visible without a `git diff` step. Reduces wasted steps and misreads of empty observations.
mechanisms.evidence: swe-agent.com/latest/config/tools/ (fetched 2026-09-21): 'state_command: "_state"' executes after every action and outputs JSON used to format prompt templates with `open_file` and `working_dir`. raw config/default.yaml (fetched 2026-09-21): next_step_no_output_template = 'Your command ran successfully and did not produce any output.'; registry variable USE_FILEMAP: 'true'; tool bundles registry, edit_anthropic, review_on_submit_m. raw tools/diff_state/config.yaml (fetched 2026-09-21): state_command '_state_diff_state' exposes the git diff in the per-turn state JSON.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's WindowEntry (src/loop/window.ts: shownFiles, notes, head 400/tail 200 output) is the analogue. Add a code-computed `state` block to every step record and to Jev's `state` object: cwd, files touched this run, `git diff --stat`, last test counts. The judge Nouls (stages/judge.ts) then ask about facts rather than raw output, and the generator gets 'ran successfully, no output' instead of an empty string. Code owns the facts; Jev consumes them.

mechanisms.name: Bash-only single tool, one process per action, linear history, sentinel finish (mini-SWE-agent)
mechanisms.what: The whole agent is ~100 lines: one `bash` tool (v2 invoked through native tool calling, v1 via a regex on a code block), every action run as an independent `subprocess`/`bash -c` with its own cwd/env, history is a flat message list, and the task ends when the output's first line is the sentinel `COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`. Limits are a cost cap (3.0), an optional step cap, a wall-time cap, and a cap on consecutive format errors (3).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: The SWE-bench maintainers use it as the 'Bash Only' baseline because the scaffold adds almost nothing, so scores track the model. It still scores >74% on Verified (74.2% with Claude 4.5 Sonnet at $0.56/issue per the Live-SWE-agent paper). Fewer moving parts means fewer harness-attributable failures and near-zero per-step overhead.
mechanisms.evidence: README (fetched 2026-09-21): 'Does not have any tools other than bash', 'doesn't even need to use the tool-calling interface of the LMs', 'completely linear history — every step of the agent just appends to the messages', 'Executes actions with subprocess.run — every action is completely independent', 'Just some 100 lines of python for the agent class', 'Scores >74% on the SWE-bench verified benchmark'. v2 migration guide mini-swe-agent.com/latest/advanced/v2_migration/ (fetched 2026-09-21): v2 default is 'Native tool calling API support' — 'Model uses native tool calling API to invoke a bash tool'; finish sentinel renamed to `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`; 'Cost tracking moved to Agent'. raw config/benchmarks/swebench.yaml (fetched 2026-09-21): step_limit 250, cost_limit 3, environment timeout 60 s, cwd /testbed, 'Directory or environment variable changes are not persistent. Every action is executed in a new subshell.' raw environments/local.py (fetched 2026-09-21): Popen shell=True, start_new_session on POSIX, 'kills the whole process group on timeout so no children are orphaned', default timeout 30, Submitted raised when output starts with the sentinel and returncode is 0. agents/default.py (fetched 2026-09-21): control flow via exceptions LimitsExceeded / TimeExceeded / FormatError / InterruptAgentFlow; max_consecutive_format_errors default 3; wall_time_limit_seconds. Live-SWE-agent arXiv 2511.13646 (fetched 2026-09-21): mini-SWE-agent + Claude 4.5 Sonnet 74.2% Verified, $0.56/issue. swebench.com/verified.html (fetched 2026-09-21) confirms an 'Agent' dropdown for mini-SWE-agent 'Bash Only' results. docs/RESEARCH.md (fetched 2026-09-19): mini-SWE-agent v2.0.0 + Claude 4.5 Sonnet (high) 71.4% on the official board.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode already matches the execution model (sandbox/run.ts: `sh -c`, detached process group, 120 s default / 600 s max, 200 KB rolling cap). Keep the action space at six and resist adding tools; the 'bash-only + sentinel' result says scaffold minimalism does not cost accuracy. The sentinel maps to JevCode's `done` action + completion Noul. Adopt the three caps as code (cost cap, wall-time cap, consecutive-format-error cap of 3 — JevCode already has max_requeries-style handling for a twice-malformed reply) and treat the generator's cost, not steps, as the primary budget in jev-on mode.

mechanisms.name: Prompted problem-solving workflow: reproduce, fix, re-run, edge cases; never edit tests; patch produced by git diff
mechanisms.what: Both harnesses hard-code the same recipe in the instance prompt: find and read the relevant code, write a script that reproduces the issue and run it, edit the source, re-run the reproduction, then test edge cases; do not modify tests or config files; produce the submission as `git diff -- <files>` and inspect it before submitting.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: A reproduction script becomes a cheap, task-specific oracle that the agent re-runs after each edit, so verification is one command rather than a full suite. Restricting edits to non-test source keeps the patch gradable and prevents 'fixing' the test.
mechanisms.evidence: swebench.yaml (fetched 2026-09-21): workflow steps 1 analyze codebase, 2 'Create script to reproduce the issue', 3 edit source, 4 'Verify fix works by running script again', 5 'Test edge cases'; 'DO NOT MODIFY: Tests, configuration files (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, etc.)'; submission is three separate commands: `git diff -- path/to/file1 path/to/file2 > patch.txt`, verify contents, `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat patch.txt`; 'Your response MUST include AT LEAST ONE bash tool call'. OpenHands SDK issue #1965 (2026-02-08, fetched 2026-09-21) lists the base system prompt sections including PROBLEM_SOLVING_WORKFLOW 'Explore/analyze/test/implement/verify; includes no-mock testing', EFFICIENCY 'Combine actions and use efficient search/explore tooling', TROUBLESHOOTING 'Backoff/diagnose repeated failures, confirm new plan', TASK_MANAGEMENT.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's synth/verify already treats tests as the oracle and produces `model_patch` with `git diff` on the harness side. Two additions, both off the critical path: (1) a code rule in the plan stage (loop/plan.ts) that a `run` of a reproduction script must precede the first `edit` in jev-on mode, with a Jev Noul 'did this run reproduce the reported failure?' feeding the plan's evidence; (2) a code guard in the applier rejecting edits under test paths unless the task explicitly asks (mirrors the DO NOT MODIFY rule) so Jev's out-of-scope Score has one fewer thing to catch.

mechanisms.name: Confirm-before-finish review checklist (SWE-agent review_on_submit_m; OpenHands Stop hook)
mechanisms.what: The first `submit` does not submit: it returns a checklist (re-run the reproduction script, delete it, `git checkout` any test files touched, then submit again). OpenHands generalises this as a `Stop` lifecycle hook that can block finishing (exit code 2) and keep the conversation going.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Catches the most common late failures (stale reproduction, leftover scratch files, accidental test edits) with one extra turn, and gives the harness a place to run deterministic checks before the trajectory ends.
mechanisms.evidence: default.yaml (fetched 2026-09-21): SUBMIT_REVIEW_MESSAGES 'Multi-step instructions requiring users to rerun reproduction scripts, remove them, revert test files, and confirm changes via git'; bundle tools/review_on_submit_m. docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/hooks.md (fetched 2026-09-21): Stop hook fires 'When agent tries to finish', blocking 'prevents the agent from finishing and the conversation continues'; only PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and Stop can block, 'Exit code 1 ... is treated as a non-blocking error', blocking requires exit code 2; hooks return JSON {"decision": "allow" | "deny", "reason": "..."} and 'The schema mirrors Claude Code's hook contract'. Pitfall recorded in software-agent-sdk PR #3183 (fetched via search 2026-09-21): 'abort run loop on repeated Stop-hook denials without progress'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's completion stage (loop/stages/complete.ts, 0.85 threshold) is the right place: before the completion Noul, run a code-owned pre-done checklist (clean `git status` for scratch files, no test-path changes, last test run newer than last edit — the engine already tracks lastChangeStep/testsCurrent) and only then ask Jev 'does the diff satisfy the task?'. Expose the same as a user `Stop` hook (JSON on stdin, exit 2 blocks), and cap repeated Stop denials at 2 so a hook cannot loop the run.

mechanisms.name: Context budget: last-N observations, head/tail elision, rolling LLM condenser, and prompt-cache-aware history
mechanisms.what: SWE-agent's LastNObservations keeps the last n observations and replaces older ones with a one-line placeholder; its `polling` parameter lets the prefix stay stable for a few steps so prompt caching survives; CacheControlHistoryProcessor marks the last 2 user/tool messages for Anthropic caching. OpenHands' LLMSummarizingCondenser triggers when the event count exceeds max_size (120), keeps the first keep_first (4) events and the recent tail verbatim, summarises the middle with a cheaper model, and targets 60 events.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Tokens per step stay flat over long runs; OpenHands reports the default condenser cuts API cost up to 2x with no accuracy loss, and the SWE-agent ablation shows last-5 beats full history (+3.0pp). Cache-aware placement keeps the stable prefix cached so each step is faster and cheaper.
mechanisms.evidence: docs.openhands.dev/sdk/arch/condenser (fetched 2026-09-21): max_size 'Event count threshold before condensation triggers (default: 120)', keep_first 'Number of initial events to preserve verbatim (default: 4)', llm 'often cheaper model than reasoning LLM', result targets '60 events total', condensation event carries forgotten_event_ids / summary / summary_offset, manual trigger on 'LLM Context Error'. arXiv 2511.03690 (fetched 2026-09-21): 'LLMSummarizingCondenser (the default condenser) has been shown to reduce API costs by up to 2× with no degradation in agent performance'. swe-agent.com/latest/reference/history_processor_config/ (fetched 2026-09-21): LastNObservations `polling: 1` 'maintains n to n+polling observations for caching', always_keep_output_for_tags {'keep_output'}, 'Using this history processor will break prompt caching'; elided text 'Old environment output: (n lines omitted)' (search result summary); CacheControlHistoryProcessor last_n_messages 2, tagged_roles ['user','tool']. Pitfall: software-agent-sdk issue #1073 'Agent got stuck in condensation loop'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's window (WINDOW_SIZE 4, head 400 / tail 200, DESIGN §6) is already the last-N design and STATUS.md shows ~12k generator tokens per step flat at step 25. Two cheap wins: (1) a `polling`-style rule that the window content only changes every k steps in jev-on mode so the Anthropic/OpenRouter cache prefix survives (code, deterministic); (2) when a step's output is elided, keep outputs Jev judged as evidence (the analogue of `keep_output` tags) — Jev has already answered that question in stages/judge.ts, so no new call. Keep compaction deterministic and cap attempts, as the coordination design already decided; do not put Jev on the compaction path.

mechanisms.name: Semantic stuck/loop detection with bounded scan (OpenHands StuckDetector) and 3-strike signatures (JevCode-comparable)
mechanisms.what: OpenHands scans the last 20 events and flags four patterns: the same action producing the same observation 4+ times, the same action erroring 3+ times, 3+ consecutive agent messages without user input, and A-B-A-B alternation for 6+ cycles; events are compared by tool name, arguments and thought, ignoring ids and metrics. Enabled by default.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Stops runaway spend on unproductive loops without an LLM call. The alternating-pattern check catches oscillation that identical-hash detectors miss.
mechanisms.evidence: Docs (fetched 2026-09-21): 'The same action produces the same observation repeatedly (4+ times)', 'The same action repeatedly results in errors (3+ times)', monologue '(3+ messages)', 'Two different action-observation pairs alternate in a ping-pong pattern (6+ cycles)', enabled by default via `stuck_detection=True`; actions compared by 'tool name, action content, and thought (ignoring IDs and metrics)'. raw stuck_detector.py (fetched 2026-09-21): `MAX_EVENTS_TO_SCAN_FOR_STUCK_DETECTION: int = 20` with comment '4 repeats × 2 events per cycle = 8 events minimum, plus buffer', thresholds read from a `StuckDetectionThresholds` object, alternating check `_event_eq(last_actions[i], last_actions[i + 2])`, context-window-error check 'TODO: blocked by' issue #282. Pitfall: OpenHands/OpenHands issue #5355 (2024-12-01, fetched 2026-09-21): agents 'getting killed with agent got stuck in a loop when they waited to long' on long-running processes.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's loop/loopdetect.ts already trips at LOOP_TRIP_COUNT 3 and, unlike OpenHands, signs failing test runs by the set of failing test ids so 6/10 → 8/10 → 9/10 never trips — keep that. Add one signature kind: alternation (A,B,A,B over run/read proposals) and the bounded 20-event scan. Route a trip to the existing replan Choice, and add the escape option 'this is legitimate waiting/polling' so Jev arbitrates the false-positive case that bit OpenHands, with a hard code cap on how many times that escape may be taken.

mechanisms.name: Parallel rollouts scored by a calibrated critic / chooser (OpenHands critic; SWE-agent RetryAgent reviewer and chooser)
mechanisms.what: Run N independent attempts and pick one. OpenHands trained a 32B critic (Qwen2.5-Coder base, TD learning with γ=0.99 from unit-test rewards, regression head) that scores each trajectory; the highest-scored patch is submitted. SWE-agent's RetryAgent does the same with prompted models: ScoreRetryLoop reviews each submission (n_sample 5 scores, accept_score threshold, failure penalty, optional std reduction) and stops on acceptance; ChooserRetryLoop collects all attempts and has a Chooser (with a Preselector when >2) pick an index; unused budget rolls into the next attempt and `min_budget_for_new_attempt` stops early.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: OpenHands went from 60.6% (single rollout) to 66.4% with five attempts on SWE-bench Verified, described as log-linear in N; the official board entry recorded 65.8% and calls it 'essentially a best@4 number'. Selection is where a calibrated decision model adds the most per dollar.
mechanisms.evidence: Blog 2025-04-17 (fetched 2026-09-21): '60.6%' single rollout to '66.4%' with five attempts, 'log-linear performance improvement'; critic from 'Qwen 2.5 Coder Instruct 32B', 'temporal difference (TD) learning objective to propagate trajectory-level success signals from unit test execution backward through each trajectory', 'regression head on top of the last layer to predict reward values', γ=0.99, terminal reward '1 for passing all tests and 0 for failing', trained with veRL on SWE-Gym rollouts 'to avoid data leakage'. HF card OpenHands/openhands-critic-32b-exp-20250417 (fetched 2026-09-21): 'select the solution from the trajectory with the highest score'; experimental 'one-step lookahead sampling' — 'evaluate multiple potential actions at each step, using the critic's scores to choose the most promising path'; 'the critic can identify declining rewards and help the agent course-correct'; caveat 'real-world generalization is not easy to guarantee'. SWE-bench/experiments PR #209 (fetched 2026-09-21): '65.8% resolved (recovered evaluation; 66.4% originally reported)', 'essentially this is a best@4 number'. raw sweagent/agent/reviewer.py (fetched 2026-09-21): Reviewer n_sample 5, accept_score, max_accepts 1, failure_score_penalty 0.0, reduce_by_std 0.0, max_len_submission 5000, min_budget_for_new_attempt 0.0; Chooser prompt = problem statement + each submission + trajectory summary, returns an index; 'If 2+ submissions are marked as submitted, only those are considered'. Pitfall: SWE-agent issue #1491 (2026-08-05, fetched 2026-09-21): Chooser.choose() 'bare except Exception' swallows TotalCostLimitExceededError and crashes with UnboundLocalError, silently defaulting to index 0.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: This is the smartest Jev placement in the whole survey: Jev is already a calibrated scorer (Choice confidence (p_max − 1/n)/(1 − 1/n); Score confidence 1 − E|k − argmax|/U_n) and JevCode already ranks 11–150 candidates with compact Nouls in chunks ≤ 50 (src/synth/rank). Extend the same machinery from candidate lines to whole patches: run 2–4 short attempts concurrently on a small task, let tests eliminate first, and ask Jev one Choice over the survivors with the diff + failing-test evidence as state. Jev never sits on the execution path — if Jev is unreachable the code falls back to 'the attempt with the most tests passing'. Budget accounting must be in code outside the chooser path (the #1491 lesson), and treat 'one-step lookahead' as a Jev Choice over K proposed actions only when the candidates differ (see the action-sampler mechanism).

mechanisms.name: Per-step action sampling with pairwise selection (SWE-agent BinaryTrajectoryComparison / AskColleagues)
mechanisms.what: At each step the model is sampled several times; unparseable and duplicate actions are dropped; if an edit is among the candidates more samples are drawn (up to max); a model then compares candidates pairwise ('first'/'second') and the winner is executed. AskColleagues instead shows the model its own n samples as a 'colleague discussion' and asks for a final action.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Spends extra compute exactly on the steps where it matters (edits, disagreement) and skips it when all samples agree, which is a cheap form of test-time scaling inside a single trajectory.
mechanisms.evidence: action_sampler.py (fetched 2026-09-21): AskColleagues `n_samples: int = 2`; BinaryTrajectoryComparison `min_n_samples: int = 4`, `max_n_samples: int = 10`, `comparison_temperature: float | None = None`; algorithm: sample min_n_samples, 'Removes unparseable completions and eliminates duplicate actions', 'If edit operations are proposed and fewer completions exist than max_n_samples, samples additional candidates', pairwise comparison reads whether 'the last line contains first or second', 'Early exit occurs when only one unique action remains after deduplication'. Configured through DefaultAgentConfig.action_sampler (swe-agent.com/latest/reference/agent_config/, fetched 2026-09-21).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Replace N−1 pairwise LLM comparisons with a single Jev Choice over the deduplicated candidate actions (n options, probability and confidence returned natively) — one Jev call instead of a chain of generator calls (inference: cheaper and faster; measure on small tasks). Trigger only when the deduped set has ≥2 members and the step is an edit/patch (the SWE-agent heuristic), so most steps pay nothing. Wire it into stages/choose.ts; the existing risk Scores still run on the chosen action, so nothing mission-critical changes.

mechanisms.name: Execution guardrails: per-command and total timeouts, interactive-command blocklist, non-interactive env, bounded re-queries (SWE-agent ToolConfig; OpenHands terminal tool)
mechanisms.what: SWE-agent runs each command with a 30 s timeout, exits after 3 consecutive timeouts or 1800 s total, blocks interactive programs (vim, vi, emacs, nano, less, tail -f, gdb, nohup, python -m venv, make) and bare REPLs (python, ipython, bash, sh, su), sets PAGER/MANPAGER/GIT_PAGER=cat, LESS=-R, PIP_PROGRESS_BAR=off, TQDM_DISABLE=1, and re-queries the model at most 3 times after a format error, blocked action or bash syntax error. OpenHands instead keeps a persistent terminal with `is_input` for sending input, control sequences (C-c, C-d ...), a `no_change_timeout_seconds` idle timeout that returns partial output, an empty command to poll, `reset` for a dead session, and output truncation with overflow saved to a file.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Hangs and pagers are the dominant wall-clock sink for shell agents; blocking them up front and returning partial output on idle keeps every step bounded. Bounded re-queries stop a malformed-output death spiral.
mechanisms.evidence: tools_config (fetched 2026-09-21): `execution_timeout: int = 30`, `install_timeout: int = 300`, `total_execution_timeout: int = 1800`, `max_consecutive_execution_timeouts: int = 3`; blocklist ['vim','vi','emacs','nano','nohup','gdb','less','tail -f','python -m venv','make']; blocklist_standalone ['python','python3','ipython','bash','sh','/bin/bash','/bin/sh','nohup','vi','vim','emacs','nano','su']; blocklist_error_template "Operation '{{action}}' is not supported by this environment."; env_variables PAGER cat, MANPAGER cat, LESS -R, PIP_PROGRESS_BAR off, TQDM_DISABLE 1, GIT_PAGER cat. agent_config (fetched 2026-09-21): `max_requeries: 3` 'Maximum number of times to requery the model after an error, such as a formatting error, a blocked action, or a bash syntax error'. raw openhands-tools terminal/definition.py (fetched 2026-09-21): `command` 'Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is -1', `is_input` 'If True, the command is an input to the running process', `timeout` optional, `reset` 'Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive', 'You can only execute one command at a time', control keys 'C-c (Ctrl+C), C-d ... UP, DOWN ... TAB, ESC, BS, ENTER', idle rule 'pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for NO_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS seconds', truncation via MAX_CMD_OUTPUT_SIZE with overflow saved to a directory.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's sandbox (run.ts 120 s default, 600 s max clamped to wall time, 200 KB rolling tail, three-pass tree kill) is stronger than SWE-agent's on cleanup but lacks the blocklist and the env scrub. Add both as code rules before the Jev risk stage (stages/risk.ts) so Jev never spends a call on `vim` or `python` with no script; add a scrubbed env with PAGER=cat and friends; add 'consecutive timeouts ≥ 3 → replan' as a loop signature. Consider returning partial output at an idle timeout (OpenHands) instead of waiting for the full 120 s — the biggest single wall-clock saver for `run` steps (inference).

mechanisms.name: Risk-tiered confirmation with a separate security analyzer and hook contract (OpenHands SDK)
mechanisms.what: Every tool call is rated low/medium/high/unknown by a SecurityAnalyzer running on a separate LLM instance, and the agent can also self-report a `security_risk` argument on the call; a ConfirmationPolicy (AlwaysConfirm, NeverConfirm, ConfirmRisky with a threshold defaulting to HIGH) decides whether the conversation stops in WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION. Users approve by calling run() or reject with `reject_pending_actions(feedback)`; PreToolUse hooks (exit 2 = deny) run before execution in command, prompt or agent mode.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Splits 'is this dangerous' from 'what should I do next', gives the human a single, named pause state, and lets rejections carry feedback so the agent changes approach instead of retrying the same action.
mechanisms.evidence: Security guide (fetched 2026-09-21): tiers LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / UNKNOWN; LLMSecurityAnalyzer 'reviews each action before execution', operates 'via a separate LLM instance'; `security_risk` parameter on tool calls; policies AlwaysConfirm(), NeverConfirm(), ConfirmRisky() 'defaults to HIGH'; pending actions set `execution_status = WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION`; `conversation.reject_pending_actions(feedback_message)`; 'Provide feedback when rejecting to help the agent try a different approach'. arXiv 2511.03690 (fetched 2026-09-21): 'SecurityAnalyzer rates each tool call as low, medium, high, or unknown risk'; agent pauses in 'WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION state until the user explicitly approves or rejects'. hooks.md (fetched 2026-09-21): PreToolUse 'Before tool execution' blocks with exit 2; modes Command / Prompt / Agent. Pitfall: software-agent-sdk PR #5110 (search 2026-09-21): 'sending a new message while WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION now rejects pending actions as superseded, and confirmation still requires run() with no new message'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode already has the stronger version: four 5-level Jev Scores (destructive, out of scope, plan mismatch, irreversible), block ≥ 0.7, ask 0.3–0.7 with no auto-approve. Borrow three things: (1) a self-reported `risk` field on the generator's tool call, passed to Jev as one more fact (never as the decision); (2) the named `WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION` state and the corner-case rule that a new user message supersedes the pending action; (3) rejection carries user feedback into the next generator prompt. Expose PreToolUse as the JSON-on-stdin hook contract the repo already adopted.

mechanisms.name: Event-sourced state with deterministic replay, pause/resume at step boundaries (OpenHands SDK V1)
mechanisms.what: All interactions are immutable events appended to a log; state is `base_state.json` plus the events directory and is rebuilt by replay; agent configuration is immutable and serialisable; `conversation.pause()` may be called from another thread, `run()` resumes, and a message may be sent while paused. Execution status is an explicit enum (IDLE, RUNNING, PAUSED, WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION, FINISHED, ...).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Crash recovery and resume become trivially correct, replay enables offline debugging and re-scoring, and the measured overhead is negligible. Production data credits the redesign with a 61% drop in system-attributable failures.
mechanisms.evidence: arXiv 2511.03690 (fetched 2026-09-21): 'all interactions as immutable events appended to a log', ConversationState with 'an append-only EventLog', recovery by 'loading base_state.json and replaying events from the directory'; agents are 'stateless, immutable specifications ... can be serialized and transmitted across process boundaries'; 'Per-event persist latency: 0.20 ms (median), 0.31 ms (P95)', 'Crash recovery ... under 20 ms' at '358 events', '380 KB median' storage; 'V1 reduces system-attributable failures by 61% (from 78.0 to 30.0 errors per 1k conversations)', V0's top failures 'HTTPStatusError (401) at 43.0 / 1k' and 'AgentRuntimeNotReadyError at 18.8 / 1k'; V1 SWE-bench Verified 72.8% with Claude Sonnet 4.5. docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/convo-pause-and-resume (fetched 2026-09-21): 'Pause the agent from another thread or after a delay using conversation.pause()', 'Resume the paused conversation ... by calling conversation.run() again', 'send a new message while paused'; statuses IDLE, RUNNING, PAUSED, FINISHED referenced via `conversation.state.execution_status`.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's checkpoint layer (run.json, atomic state.json + prev, steps.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, jev.jsonl, generator.jsonl; DESIGN §9, §9.1 step commit rule) is already event-sourced per step. Two upgrades: (1) a replay mode that rebuilds state from steps.jsonl + decisions.jsonl without calling Jev or the generator — instant, offline, and the fastest way to iterate on engine rules and TUI rendering on small runs; (2) an explicit execution-status enum and the rule 'pause takes effect at the step commit point; a new user message during a pending confirmation supersedes it' for the coordination design's pause points. Keep Jev out of persistence entirely.

mechanisms.name: Delegation and bounded parallelism: sub-agents, parallel tool calls, workflow orchestration (OpenHands)
mechanisms.what: The SDK executes multiple tool calls from one LLM response concurrently under `tool_concurrency_limit` (default 1); the TaskToolSet runs named sub-agents synchronously in their own persisted conversations and returns a compact TaskObservation; sub-agents can be defined as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under `.agents/agents/`; the `workflow` tool runs LLM-written orchestration code with `run_agent`, `map_agents`, `reduce_agent`, `pipeline` and a `max_concurrency` (default 8, 2–4 advised for LLM-heavy work); `ask_oracle` consults a stronger saved LLM profile for a second opinion; the original platform's AgentDelegateAction hands sub-tasks to specialised agents.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Read-only fan-out (search, review, audit) parallelises safely; each sub-agent keeps its own context so the parent stays small; explicit concurrency ceilings keep rate limits and shared-file conflicts under control.
mechanisms.evidence: parallel-tool-execution.md (fetched 2026-09-21): `tool_concurrency_limit` default `1`; '2-8: Moderate parallelism—good for most use cases', '>8: High parallelism—only for I/O-heavy workloads with independent tools'; avoid 'Tools modifying shared state', 'Operations writing to identical files', 'one tool's output feeds into another'; safe: 'Running multiple read-only operations simultaneously' and 'Delegating to multiple sub-agents at once'. task-tool-set.md (fetched 2026-09-21): 'The parent blocks until the sub-agent finishes and returns its result'; TaskObservation fields task_id, subagent, status, text; each sub-agent conversation 'persisted to disk'; 'TaskToolSet is designed for sequential blocking tasks'. agent-file-based.md (fetched 2026-09-21): frontmatter name (required), description, tools, model ('inherit'), skills, max_iteration_per_run, permission_mode (always_confirm, never_confirm, confirm_risky), hooks, mcp_servers; discovery `{project}/.agents/agents/*.md` then `.openhands/agents`, then user-level; project overrides user. raw tools/workflow/definition.py (fetched 2026-09-21): 'Run a dynamic workflow written as Python orchestration code' for 'codebase-wide audits, independent plan reviews, security sweeps'; script 'must define async def main(wf):'; `max_concurrency` 1–64 default 8, 'Consider 2–4 for LLM-heavy workflows to avoid hitting API rate limits'; scripts 'should not read or write files, run shell commands, or perform the engineering work directly'. raw tools/ask_oracle/definition.py (fetched 2026-09-21): 'Ask the Oracle for a second opinion. The Oracle is a smart model intended to help with difficult reasoning'. arXiv 2407.16741 (fetched 2026-09-21): AgentDelegateAction lets an agent 'delegate a specific subtask to another agent'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Maps onto the coordination design's lanes/sub-agents (docs/COORDINATION-DESIGN.md). Code rules: parallel lanes only for read-only work or provably disjoint file sets (computed from the plan's file lists), concurrency 2–4, each lane its own checkpoint dir and its own window, and a summary-only return to the parent. Jev's role: a Choice on 'which lane's patch to merge' and a Noul on 'do these lanes touch overlapping files?' when the static check is ambiguous — advisory, never gating merge correctness (tests do). For onboarding, `.agents/agents/*.md` and `.openhands/agents/*.md` are import formats to read alongside CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. `ask_oracle` is the OpenHands analogue of asking Jev — in JevCode the generator can already be told to defer a decision to Jev.

mechanisms.name: Planning surfaces that cost no sandbox round-trip: TaskTracker, Think and Finish tools (OpenHands)
mechanisms.what: TaskTracker has two commands, `view` and `plan`, over a list of {title, notes, status ∈ todo|in_progress|done} persisted to TASKS.json, with guidance to keep one task in progress and not to mark done while tests fail; Think is a parameterless no-op that logs a thought ('Your thought has been logged'); Finish takes a final message and ends the run.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Gives the model a place to plan or reason without executing anything, and gives the harness a machine-readable plan with per-item status to judge progress against. Explicit finish avoids sentinel parsing.
mechanisms.evidence: task_tracker/definition.py (fetched 2026-09-21): use for 'Multi-phase development work', 'Complex implementation tasks'; not for 'Single atomic tasks that require no decomposition', 'Trivial operations'; statuses "todo", "in_progress", "done"; 'Limit active work to ONE task at any given time'; do not mark done when 'Test suites are failing'; command `view` or `plan`; persisted to 'save_dir/TASKS.json'. builtins/think.py (fetched 2026-09-21): 'logging thoughts without making changes', use to 'brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug', returns 'Your thought has been logged', raises ValueError if given parameters. builtins/finish.py (fetched 2026-09-21): 'Signals the completion of the current task or conversation. Use this tool when: - You have successfully completed the user's requested task - You cannot proceed further', single parameter `message`. Default preset (raw tools/preset/default.py, fetched 2026-09-21): TerminalTool, FileEditorTool, TaskTrackerTool, BrowserToolSet (off in `cli_mode`), FinishTool when a response schema is set; condenser 'Shared with spawned sub-agents'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode already keeps a persistent plan with evidence (loop/plan.ts) and has `done`. Make the plan TASKS-shaped (title/status/evidence) so the completion stage can ask Jev one Noul per open item instead of one global 'is it done?' — same number of tokens, sharper answer. Add a `note` (think) action that records reasoning into the step record without a sandbox run: it costs a generator call but no execution, no judge Noul, and no test run, so it is the cheapest possible step (inference on cost).

mechanisms.name: Repository knowledge and persistent memory injection: skills with keyword/path triggers, two-tier MEMORY.md (OpenHands)
mechanisms.what: Skills are Markdown with YAML frontmatter: repository skills (trigger null, typically AGENTS.md) always load; knowledge skills fire on keywords in the user message; task skills fire semantically with structured inputs; path skills fire when the agent touches files matching a glob and are injected into the tool result rather than the prompt. Persistent memory is two tiers (`~/.openhands/memory/` and `<workspace>/.openhands/memory/`), each with a curated MEMORY.md — the only file injected, capped at about 6,000 characters combined, oldest lines dropped first — plus on-demand daily logs; the agent writes memory itself near the end of a task.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Project conventions and prior lessons reach the model only when relevant, so the prompt stays small; the cap keeps per-step tokens bounded; legacy `.openhands/microagents/` remains readable, which matters for importing existing setups.
mechanisms.evidence: skill.md (fetched 2026-09-21): Repository Skills 'trigger: None' stored in 'AGENTS.md at the repo root'; Knowledge Skills via `KeywordTrigger` ('kubernetes', 'k8s'); Task Skills via `TaskTrigger`; Path Skills via `PathTrigger` 'injected into the tool result, not model-invocable'; discovery `.agents/skills/`. docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/skill (fetched 2026-09-21): 'Both the legacy .openhands/skills/ and .openhands/microagents/ directories remain supported, but use .agents/skills/ for new skills'. persistent-memory.md (fetched 2026-09-21): tiers `~/.openhands/memory/` and `<workspace>/.openhands/memory/`; 'MEMORY.md – a curated index of durable facts. This is the only file injected into the prompt'; daily logs `YYYY-MM-DD.md`; injected as a `<MEMORY_CONTEXT>` block when `load_memory=True`; 'record durable, broadly useful facts in MEMORY.md near the end of a task'; combined indexes 'capped at ~6,000 characters', 'whole lines are dropped from the top of each over-budget tier'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Defines the import surface for the onboarding wizard (tui/onboarding): read CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .agents/skills/**/SKILL.md / .openhands/skills / .openhands/microagents / .agents/agents/*.md and ~/.openhands/memory/MEMORY.md, normalise into JevCode's config dir, and preserve trigger metadata. At run time compute keyword and path triggers in code (cheap, deterministic); ask Jev only the ambiguous question 'is this skill relevant to the current step?' when several fire, and hard-cap injected text (6k chars is a sane default) so the flat tokens-per-step property holds.

mechanisms.name: Runtime tool self-evolution on top of a bash-only scaffold (Live-SWE-agent)
mechanisms.what: Starting from mini-SWE-agent, the prompt tells the model it may write its own Python tool scripts into the working directory (they 'do not need to be general'), and after each step it is asked to reflect on whether a tool would help; tools created are edit helpers, context-aware search, and issue-specific analysers.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Reported 77.4% on SWE-bench Verified with Claude 4.5 Sonnet versus 74.2% for mini-SWE-agent (cost $0.68 vs $0.56 per issue) and 45.8% vs 43.6% on SWE-bench Pro, with no offline training; multi-step bash chains get replaced by one tool call, which also saves turns.
mechanisms.evidence: arXiv 2511.13646 (fetched 2026-09-21): 'starts with the most basic agent scaffold with only access to bash tools'; prompt: agent 'can also create your own tools in Python to help with your workflow', tools 'do not need to be general'; per-step reflection 'Reflect on the previous trajectories and decide if there are any tools you can create to help you with the current task'; results: Live-SWE-agent 77.4% vs mini-SWE-agent 74.2% Verified (Claude 4.5 Sonnet), $0.68 vs $0.56 per issue; SWE-bench Pro 45.8% vs 43.6%; vs Darwin-Gödel Machine on a 60-problem subset 65.0% (GPT-5-Mini) vs 53.3% with '1,231 hours offline training'; example search tool 'ignores irrelevant folders (__pycache__ and node_modules) and hidden folders (.git)'. docs/RESEARCH.md (fetched 2026-09-19): live-SWE-agent + Claude 4.5 Opus 79.2% is a top official Verified entry.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Opt-in, off the critical path: allow the generator to `write` helper scripts only under the run's scratch directory (already workspace-confined by the sandbox and excluded from `git diff`), and add a cheap Jev Noul at replan time — 'would a reusable helper speed the remaining plan?' — rather than a reflection prompt every step (inference: the per-step reflection is where the +$0.12/issue goes). Test on small tasks first; do not enable in bench arms until measured.

mechanisms.name: Compact file views: filemap skeletons and file-list-only search (SWE-agent)
mechanisms.what: `filemap` parses a Python file with tree-sitter and prints it with every function body of 5+ lines replaced by '... eliding lines a-b ...', keeping signatures and short bodies; it is on by default (USE_FILEMAP true). Directory search returns only the list of files with a match.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: A large file becomes a navigable outline in one observation instead of several 100-line windows; search results stay short enough to reason over. Both cut tokens and steps in the exploration phase, which is where most steps go.
mechanisms.evidence: filemap script (fetched 2026-09-21): tree-sitter query '(function_definition body: (_) @body)', elides bodies where 'node.end_point[0] - node.start_point[0] >= 5', marker '... eliding lines {start+1}-{end+1} ...', 'Currently Python only'. raw config/default.yaml (fetched 2026-09-21): registry variable `USE_FILEMAP: 'true'`. raw tools/search/config.yaml (fetched 2026-09-21): search_dir 'searches for search_term in all files in dir', find_file, search_file. swe-agent.com/latest/background/aci/ (fetched 2026-09-21): 'we simply list each file that had at least one match'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Add a `read` mode `outline` in the applier that elides bodies ≥ 5 lines (a regex/indent-based version for Python and JS/TS is enough; no tree-sitter dependency, keeping the zero-runtime-dependency rule) and let the context stage show outlines for files Jev selected but the generator has not opened. Pure code, deterministic, immediately measurable as fewer tokens per context step.

mechanisms.name: Massively parallel sandboxed execution and global spend caps for iteration (SWE-ReX; mini-SWE-agent batch runner)
mechanisms.what: SWE-ReX is a runtime that runs agent commands in local, Docker, Modal or AWS Fargate sandboxes behind one API, detects command completion, returns exit codes, and supports many parallel shell sessions; mini-SWE-agent's batch runner parallelises instances with `--workers` and enforces process-wide `MSWEA_GLOBAL_COST_LIMIT` / `MSWEA_GLOBAL_CALL_LIMIT`.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Fast iteration on small task sets comes from running several tasks concurrently under one budget rather than from bigger benchmarks; the maintainers used this to evaluate 'a few hundred trajectories with ease'.
mechanisms.evidence: SWE-ReX README (fetched 2026-09-21): 'a runtime interface for interacting with sandboxed shell environments', 'Support fast, massively parallel agent runs (which made evaluating on large benchmarks a breeze)', demo of '30 SWE-bench instances in parallel', 'SWE-ReX will recognize when commands are finished, extract the output and exit code', 'multiple such shell sessions in parallel'; deployments Docker, Modal, AWS Fargate, Daytona (WIP). SWE-agent v1.0.0 release (2025-02-13, fetched 2026-09-21): 'Fast, massively parallel code execution with SWE-ReX', 'New command line trajectory inspector to scroll few hundreds of trajectories with ease'. mini-swe-agent.com/latest/usage/swebench/ (fetched 2026-09-21): `-w, --workers` 'Number of worker threads for parallel processing (default: 1)'; env `MSWEA_GLOBAL_CALL_LIMIT`, `MSWEA_GLOBAL_COST_LIMIT`; results `preds.json` + `{instance_id}/{instance_id}.traj.json`; evaluate with `sb-cli submit swe-bench_verified test --predictions_path preds.json`; Docker env 'x86 Linux only'. Pitfalls from mini-swe-agent releases (fetched 2026-09-21): v2.4.4 'Fixed shared config mutation in benchmark workers', v2.4.1 'kill local process group on timeout', v2.4.6 'count billed calls that fail to parse against cost_limit'.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's bench already has `--concurrency N`, per-worker directories and one root SpendMeter (DESIGN §13). For the user's 'test on small stuff and iterate' loop, add a `jevcode bench --quick` preset: 3–5 checked-in tasks, concurrency 3, mocked Jev/generator by default, a low live spend cap, and the replay mode from the event-sourcing mechanism so most iterations run with zero API calls. Deep-copy per-worker config and count unparseable-but-billed generator calls against the cap (the two mini-swe-agent regressions).

speed_tricks: Combine several shell commands into one action; OpenHands' EFFICIENCY prompt section exists because each action is a full LLM round-trip (issue #1965; agents.buttonscli.com field guide summary, 2026-09-21).

Keep the tool surface tiny (bash-only + sentinel, or JevCode's six actions): mini-SWE-agent shows the scaffold adds nothing measurable, and fewer tools means shorter system prompts and fewer format errors (github.com/swe-agent/mini-swe-agent, 2026-09-21).

Use native tool calling for the action channel (mini-SWE-agent v2 switched from regex-parsed code blocks) and cap consecutive format errors at 3 so a malformed reply costs at most three cheap re-queries (v2 migration guide; agents/default.py, 2026-09-21).

Budget by cost, not steps: mini-SWE-agent's swebench config is step_limit 250 with cost_limit 3; SWE-agent per_instance_cost_limit 3.0; global MSWEA_GLOBAL_COST_LIMIT across workers (mini-swe-agent.com/latest/usage/swebench/, 2026-09-21).

Protect the prompt-cache prefix: SWE-agent's CacheControlHistoryProcessor tags the last 2 user/tool messages and warns that LastNObservations 'will break prompt caching' unless `polling` keeps history stable for several steps (history_processor_config, 2026-09-21).

Summarise rather than truncate when the event count passes a threshold: OpenHands' default condenser (max_size 120, keep_first 4, target 60, cheaper summariser LLM) is credited with up to 2x lower API cost at equal accuracy (arXiv 2511.03690; sdk/arch/condenser, 2026-09-21).

Run read-only tool calls from one response concurrently with a small ceiling (OpenHands tool_concurrency_limit 2–8; workflow max_concurrency 2–4 for LLM-heavy fan-out) and never parallelise writes to the same files (parallel-tool-execution.md; workflow/definition.py, 2026-09-21).

Show outlines, not files: filemap elides function bodies ≥ 5 lines; the 100-line viewer window beat both 30 lines and full files in the ACI ablation (12.7% full file vs 18.0%) (tools/filemap; arXiv 2405.15793, 2026-09-21).
Return only the list of matching files from search; showing per-match context dropped SWE-bench Lite from 18.0% to 12.0% (arXiv 2405.15793, 2026-09-21).

Kill hangs before they start: set PAGER/MANPAGER/GIT_PAGER=cat, LESS=-R, PIP_PROGRESS_BAR=off, TQDM_DISABLE=1 and block vim/vi/emacs/nano/less/tail -f/gdb/nohup and bare python/ipython/bash/sh/su; 30 s per-command timeout, exit after 3 consecutive timeouts (swe-agent.com/latest/reference/tools_config/, 2026-09-21).

Return partial output on idle instead of waiting for the hard timeout: OpenHands' terminal pauses after `no_change_timeout_seconds` without new output and lets the agent poll with an empty command or send C-c (terminal/definition.py, 2026-09-21).

Make a reproduction script early and re-run it as the oracle after each edit; run targeted tests, and run the full suite only at the pre-finish checklist (mini-swe-agent swebench.yaml; SWE-agent review_on_submit_m, 2026-09-21). (inference on 'targeted first')

Spend extra samples only where they pay: SWE-agent's BinaryTrajectoryComparison draws more candidates only when an edit is proposed and exits early when all samples are identical (action_sampler.py, 2026-09-21). For JevCode, one Jev Choice over deduped candidates replaces N−1 pairwise LLM comparisons (inference).

Best-of-N over whole attempts is the biggest single accuracy lever (60.6% → 66.4% at N=5) but multiplies cost; use N=2–4 on small tasks and let tests eliminate before the critic ranks (openhands.dev blog 2025-04-17; SWE-bench/experiments PR #209, 2026-09-21).

Persist every event (0.20 ms median per event, <20 ms crash recovery) and replay from the log to iterate on engine and TUI rules with zero API calls (arXiv 2511.03690, 2026-09-21). (inference for the replay-as-test-harness use)

Run several small tasks concurrently under one global cap rather than one big benchmark: mini-SWE-agent `--workers`, SWE-ReX '30 SWE-bench instances in parallel' (mini-swe-agent.com; SWE-ReX README, 2026-09-21).

Give the model a no-execution step (OpenHands Think tool, TaskTracker plan) so reasoning and planning turns skip the sandbox, the judge and the test run (think.py; task_tracker/definition.py, 2026-09-21). (inference on cost)
Inject repo knowledge only when triggered (keyword or path) and cap injected memory (~6,000 chars) so tokens per step stay flat (sdk/arch/skill.md; persistent-memory.md, 2026-09-21).
pitfalls: Loop detection false positives: OpenHands killed agents that were legitimately polling long-running processes ('agent got stuck in a loop' while waiting), and detector thresholds were not tunable at the time (OpenHands/OpenHands issue #5355, 2024-12-01, fetched 2026-09-21). JevCode's failure-identity signatures avoid the test-progress case; add an explicit 'legitimate waiting' escape with a hard cap.

Budget enforcement inside a judge/chooser path can be silently defeated: SWE-agent's Chooser wrapped the model call in a bare `except Exception`, swallowed TotalCostLimitExceededError, crashed with UnboundLocalError and fell back to index 0 (SWE-agent issue #1491, 2026-08-05, fetched 2026-09-21). Keep cost ceilings in code outside any Jev/LLM selection path.

Rewriting history breaks prompt caching: 'Using this history processor will break prompt caching (as the history of every query will change every time due to the elided observations)' (swe-agent.com history_processor_config, 2026-09-21).
Condensation can loop: 'Agent got stuck in condensation loop' (software-agent-sdk issue #1073, via search 2026-09-21); cap compaction attempts and never compact twice without a new event.

Parallel tool execution is unsafe for tools 'modifying shared state', 'writing to identical files', or where 'one tool's output feeds into another' (parallel-tool-execution.md, 2026-09-21); parallelise reads and disjoint-file lanes only.
Both too little and too much context hurt: 30-line windows (14.3%) and full files (12.7%) both lost to 100 lines (18.0%); full history lost to last-5 observations (arXiv 2405.15793, 2026-09-21).

Learned or prompted rerankers do not automatically generalise: OpenHands notes 'real-world generalization is not easy to guarantee' for its critic (HF card, 2026-09-21); the repo's research also records SWE-RM naming calibration as a requirement. Tests remain the primary oracle; Jev ranks among test-surviving candidates.

Billed-but-unparseable model calls must count against the cost cap (mini-swe-agent v2.4.6 fix), per-worker config must not be shared/mutated across benchmark workers (v2.4.4), and timeouts must kill the whole process group (v2.4.1) (github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/releases, 2026-09-21).

Sentinel-style finishing has sharp edges: 'Do not combine it with any other command ... After this command, you cannot continue working on this task' (mini.yaml, 2026-09-21); prefer an explicit `done` action with a pre-finish checklist.

Per-action subshells forget cwd and env: 'Directory or environment variable changes are not persistent. Every action is executed in a new subshell' — commands must be prefixed each time (swebench.yaml, 2026-09-21); tell the generator this explicitly.

A new user message during a pending confirmation was previously misread as approval; the fix makes it supersede and reject the pending action, with approval still requiring run() with no new message (software-agent-sdk PR #5110, 2026-09-21). Define this corner case explicitly in the TUI pause/confirm model.
Stop-hook denials without progress can spin the run loop (software-agent-sdk PR #3183 'abort run loop on repeated Stop-hook denials without progress', 2026-09-21); cap repeated denials.

Container defaults do not fit the reference machine: mini-SWE-agent's default environment is Docker 'x86 Linux only' and SWE-bench grading needs Docker or a remote evaluator (mini-swe-agent.com/latest/usage/swebench/, 2026-09-21; docs/RESEARCH.md §0.4, 2026-09-19).
macOS `sed -i` needs `sed -i ''` (mini.yaml, 2026-09-21) — relevant if the generator is taught heredoc/sed editing instead of the exact-match `edit` action.

Runtime tool self-evolution adds cost and attack surface (+$0.12/issue in Live-SWE-agent) and writes executables into the working tree; keep it opt-in and scratch-dir-confined (arXiv 2511.13646, 2026-09-21).
High default fan-out hits rate limits: the OpenHands workflow tool defaults to max_concurrency 8 but advises 2–4 for LLM-heavy workflows (workflow/definition.py, 2026-09-21).
Interactive programs and pagers hang bash agents; without the blocklist and PAGER=cat the per-command timeout is the only defence (tools_config, 2026-09-21).

Not verifiable today: exact OpenHands system prompt text (404 on both GitHub paths) and the numeric defaults in StuckDetectionThresholds (docs give 4/3/3/6; code reads them from a config object); the third-party claim that thresholds are 'hardcoded' is outdated relative to current source.
