mechanisms.name: Bounded, isolated child agents that return a structured summary (depth-1, capped, summary-only)
mechanisms.what: Every 2025–2026 harness runs helpers as separate sessions with their own context, explicit turn/time caps, no recursion, and returns only a final result to the parent. Goose: 25 max turns (`GOOSE_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS`), 5-minute default timeout, subagents cannot spawn subagents or modify extensions, 'Summary Only' return; Roo: `new_task` with a `mode`, isolated history, result via `attempt_completion.result`; Amp: Search/Oracle/Librarian/Read-Thread subagents, main agent gets only the final summary; Kilo: `mode: "subagent"`, `steps` cap; Devin: each managed Devin in its own VM, coordinator can sleep/terminate/message children and see per-child ACU.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Parallelism without context pollution; hard caps make runaway cost impossible; summary-only return keeps the parent's prompt (and its cache prefix) small and stable.
mechanisms.evidence: Goose subagents page (fetched 2026-09-21): "5-minute default", "Max Turns: 25", "Set `GOOSE_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS` to change the default max turns for all subagents", cannot "create additional subagents to prevent infinite recursion", cannot "enable, disable, or modify extensions to avoid conflicts with the main session", "Summary Only: Get just the final result to keep your conversation clean". Env page https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/environment-variables/ (2026-09-21): GOOSE_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS default 25. Secondary: https://www.nickyt.co/blog/advent-of-ai-day-11-goose-subagents/ (post 2025-12-17, fetched 2026-09-21): "max 10 concurrent subagents (hard-coded)" — not on the official page, treat as unverified. Roo https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/features/boomerang-tasks (2026-09-21): "Each subtask operates in complete isolation with its own conversation history. It does not automatically inherit the parent's context."; "This summary is passed via the `result` parameter of the `attempt_completion` tool"; "By default, you must approve the creation and completion of each subtask." Amp https://ampcode.com/docs/models-and-subagents (2026-09-21): "you can't guide them mid-task, and they start with the instructions and context the main agent gives them rather than the full conversation". Kilo https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-subagents (2026-09-21): `steps` = "maximum agentic iterations before forcing a text-only response". Devin https://cognition.com/blog/devin-can-now-manage-devins (2026-03-19, fetched 2026-09-21): "Each managed Devin is a full Devin, running in its own isolated virtual machine"; "put child sessions to sleep or terminate them"; "monitor ACU consumption".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's parallel unit already exists: shadow lanes (src/synth/sieve/lanes.ts: candidate_file / worktree / copy / inplace) and the llm-jev sample round. Promote a lane run to a first-class child with its own step/turn/wall/spend caps (defaults in the Goose range: 25 turns, 5 min) and a structured return {claim, evidence, filesTouched, testResult} — never prose. The parent asks Jev Nouls over that structured summary at the join; Jev is not on the child's critical path. Enforce depth 1 (children cannot spawn) and cap concurrency (Goose 10 / Kilo 4 versions) in COORDINATION-DESIGN §6. Bench at n=3 lanes on QuixBugs, not comprehensively.

mechanisms.name: Orchestrator that cannot touch the workspace (dispatch, judge, merge only)
mechanisms.what: Roo's Orchestrator mode deliberately has no file, MCP or command tools; it only splits work, delegates via `new_task`, and consumes subtask summaries. Goose's RPI pattern likewise keeps the planner in a separate session from the implementer.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Prevents 'context poisoning' of the coordinator with raw tool output, keeps its prompt tiny and cache-stable, and makes the merge step the single place where conflicts are decided.
mechanisms.evidence: Roo boomerang page (fetched 2026-09-21): the Orchestrator mode intentionally cannot read/write files, call MCPs, or run commands; this design "helps prevent context poisoning". Goose RPI https://goose-docs.ai/docs/tutorials/rpi/ (2026-09-21): "It's important to do each phase in a new session to keep the LLM laser focused on only the task at hand. One goal per session!"; research phase spawns "find_files", "analyze_code", "find_patterns" subagents in parallel.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: In JevCode the orchestrator is code + Jev, which already never writes code. Keep it that way for children: the parent loop only (a) proposes the split (code: per failing test / per file, as JEV-ONLY.md's outer loop already does), (b) asks Jev which split to run (Choice), (c) merges lane patches with git and asks Jev to arbitrate only on textual conflicts. No generator turn in the parent means zero LLM latency on the join path.

mechanisms.name: Shadow-git checkpoints after every tool use, with split restore (files / task / both)
mechanisms.what: Cline and Roo commit the whole workspace (including untracked files) to a separate shadow repository after each tool use and before each modification, then offer three restores: files only, conversation only, or both, with a diff view. Roo disables the feature when nested .git repos are present and dedupes snapshots within one streaming operation.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Cheap (a git commit), captures files the user's git ignores, and lets a human or the harness rewind either the workspace or the transcript independently — the primitive behind safe parallel lanes and /undo.
mechanisms.evidence: Cline (fetched 2026-09-21): "After each tool use (file edits, commands, etc.), Cline commits the current state of your files to this shadow repo."; "Checkpoints capture everything, including files not tracked by Git."; restores "Restore Files", "Restore Task Only", "Restore Files & Task"; for large repos "checkpoints may use significant storage and slow down Cline". Roo https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/features/checkpoints (2026-09-21): "Checkpoints are recorded when tasks begin and before file modifications."; "If nested Git repositories are detected in your workspace, checkpoints are disabled."; prevents "duplicate checkpointing within a single streaming operation".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode has atomic state.json checkpoints, steps.jsonl and src/undo (patch-based), and lanes reset with `git checkout -- . && git clean -fdq`. Add a shadow repo (GIT_DIR under <runDir>/tmp, work-tree = workspace, harness git with hooks disabled as DESIGN §8 already does) committed after each applied action; wire /undo and /rewind to the three-way restore and show the diff in the Review pane. Untracked-file capture matters for llm-jev's L2 reproduction scripts. Disable on nested repos; skip when the workspace exceeds the existing 50 MB copy threshold. No Jev call involved — pure speed/safety.

mechanisms.name: Cache-stable context editing: append-only prefix, evict stale file reads, verbatim tail, batch eviction at step boundaries
mechanisms.what: Cline replaces older copies of a re-read file with the latest version instead of truncating history, explicitly to preserve prompt-cache hits. TokenPilot (EMNLP 2026) formalises it: normalise tool output at the ingestion gate so the prefix stays stable, and evict segments only on a conservative batch schedule when their task relevance expires. Every harness keeps a verbatim tail (Kilo `tail_turns` 2; Codex 20k tokens of recent user messages; OpenCode last 40k tokens of tool output) and triggers compaction at a threshold (Goose 0.8, Amp Neo 90%, Claude Code ~95%, Kilo reserved buffer min(20k, max_output)).
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Compaction that rewrites earlier messages invalidates the KV/prefix cache and can cost more than it saves; ingestion-time normalisation plus rare, batched eviction keeps 60–87% cost reductions while preserving hits.
mechanisms.evidence: Cline blog (fetched 2026-09-21): "removing these older outdated file reads, leaving only the latest version of the file in context"; "aggressively truncating older messages can break the cache, potentially increasing costs on subsequent turns"; "prioritizes removing file redundancy first, maximizing cache hits and cost savings". TokenPilot https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17016 (submitted 2026-06-15, fetched 2026-09-21): "unconstrained sequence mutations alter layouts, introducing prefix mismatches and cache invalidation"; Ingestion-Aware Compaction to "stabilize prompt prefixes and eliminate open-world environmental noise at the ingestion gate"; Lifecycle-Aware Eviction with a "conservative batch-turn schedule"; cost −61%/−56% isolated, −61%/−87% continuous. Kilo https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/context/context-condensing (2026-09-21): `compaction.tail_turns` default 2; buffer "min(20,000, model_max_output_tokens)". Goose smart-context page https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/sessions/smart-context-management/ (2026-09-21): `GOOSE_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD` default 0.8; "goose summarizes older tool call outputs in the background while keeping recent calls in full detail". Amp Neo https://ampcode.com/news/neo (2026-05-06): "Compaction now runs automatically when the context window is 90% full." badlogic gist https://gist.github.com/badlogic/cd2ef65b0697c4dbe2d13fbecb0a0a5f (2025-12-02, fetched 2026-09-21): Codex keeps "recent user messages (up to 20k tokens)"; OpenCode protects "last 40k tokens of tool output".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: COORDINATION-DESIGN §8 already plans tiered history (≤12), fileCache (≤16) and `context.compaction: 'code'` by default. Make the code compactor ingestion-gated: strip ANSI/timestamps, dedupe repeated test output and cap tool results when they enter history (Goose spills >200,000 chars to a temp file — GOOSE_MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_SIZE); keep system/tools/plan byte-stable; evict superseded file versions in a batch at a step boundary, not per step; keep 2 verbatim turns; trigger at 80–90% or the reserved-output buffer. Jev decides *which* cached files are still needed (Nouls) at the end of a step while tests run — off the critical path — code performs the eviction.

mechanisms.name: Prompt-cache wiring: tools→system→messages hierarchy, a breakpoint on the message tail, deferred tools, stable tool_choice; OpenRouter auto-cache for Z.AI/GLM
mechanisms.what: Anthropic caches a prefix hierarchy (tools → system → messages) with up to 4 explicit breakpoints; put one on the last tool, one on the system prompt, one on the last message so the growing history is read from cache each step. Changing tool definitions invalidates everything; changing `tool_choice` or thinking/effort params invalidates the messages cache; deferred tools (`defer_loading`, tool search) append as `tool_reference` blocks and preserve the prefix. Reads cost 0.1× (0.025× on Fable 5.1), writes 1.25× (5-min) / 2× (1-h); minimum 1,024 tokens on Sonnet 5, 512 on Fable 5.1; 20-block lookback. OpenRouter: Z.AI, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Grok, Moonshot and Groq cache automatically and report `cached_tokens`; sticky routing maximises hits.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: For a 25-step run the same ~10k-token prefix is re-sent every step; with correct breakpoints most of it bills at 10% and returns faster (prefill skipped).
mechanisms.evidence: Anthropic tool-use caching page (fetched 2026-09-21): "Place `cache_control: {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"}` on the last tool in your `tools` array"; hierarchy "`tools` → `system` → `messages`"; table: "Modifying tool definitions | Entire cache", "Changing `tool_choice` | Messages cache", "Changing thinking parameters | Messages cache always…"; deferred tools: "The prefix is untouched, so prompt caching is preserved"; "limit of four breakpoints". Prompt caching page https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching (2026-09-21): minimums 512 (Fable 5.1) / 1,024 (Sonnet 5); "5-minute cache write tokens are 1.25 times the base input tokens price; 1-hour cache write tokens are 2 times…; Cache read tokens are 0.1 times"; "The lookback window is 20 blocks"; usage fields `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`. OpenRouter https://openrouter.ai/docs/features/prompt-caching (2026-09-21): "OpenAI, DeepSeek, Grok, Moonshot AI, Groq, and Z.AI automatically enable prompt caching"; Z.AI "Cache reads are reported in the `cached_tokens` field of `prompt_tokens_details`"; "provider sticky routing to maximize cache hits"; `cache_discount` field.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Already wired: src/provider/anthropic.ts:87 marks the system prompt and :98 the last tool; src/provider/openrouter.ts:273-278 reads `cached_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens`; defaults.ts has cache prices. Missing: (1) a third breakpoint on the last user/tool-result block so history is cached across steps; (2) keep `tool_choice` constant within a phase (llm-jev forces `propose_fix` — do not alternate with auto per step, or place a breakpoint before the switch); (3) never change `reasoning`/effort mid-run; (4) show cache-hit % in the status bar and `/cost`. For GLM 5.3 Flash via OpenRouter, LLM-JEV-DESIGN open question #2 is answered: Z.AI caches automatically and reports it — but N simultaneous samples of one prefix will mostly miss because the cache is written by the first request to finish [inference]; the existing stagger (sample 0 first, 1..N−1 after) on the QuixBugs class should be measured for `cached_tokens` on the later samples and extended to the repository class if it hits.

mechanisms.name: Multi-model routing: lead/worker, cheap model for compaction and search, strongest model as an on-demand oracle
mechanisms.what: Amp's Dial (low/medium/high/ultra) binds "a model, reasoning effort, system prompt, tools, and oracle" per level and runs Search on a fast model while Oracle is a strong reasoning model invoked only for hard planning; Kilo lets `agent.compaction.model` be a cheaper model (Roo deliberately refuses this); Goose's lead/worker switches from a planning model to an execution model after the first turns with failure-based fallback; Trae's Lakeview summarises steps with a dedicated LLM.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Most steps are mechanical; paying the strong model only when a router says the step is hard cuts cost and latency without a quality cliff.
mechanisms.evidence: Amp models page (fetched 2026-09-21): modes `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`; "Each mode combines a model, reasoning effort, system prompt, tools, and oracle"; subagents Search ("retrieves relevant code quickly"), Oracle ("handles difficult reasoning and planning"), Librarian, Read Thread; Amp "chooses subagents automatically for suitable tasks, mostly in `medium` mode". Kilo condensing doc (2026-09-21): `{"agent": {"compaction": {"model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"}}}`; "If no compaction agent is set, the current session's model is used." Roo condensing https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/features/intelligent-context-condensing (2026-09-21): "Condensing always uses your active conversation provider/model" (to avoid degradation with tool calls). Goose: `GOOSE_LEAD_MODEL`, `GOOSE_LEAD_PROVIDER` appear in secondary sources (docs.z.ai goose page, search 2026-09-21); turn counts / failure-threshold defaults NOT confirmed on any primary page — inference only. Trae README https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bytedance/trae-agent/main/README.md (2026-09-21): `enable_lakeview: true`, "short and concise summarisation for agent steps".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's modes are already a router, and Jev's calibrated probability is a better trigger than Amp's heuristics: keep GLM 5.3 Flash as the worker; when Jev's rank/judge confidence falls in its documented noisy band (0.55–0.80) or the loop detector trips, escalate one sample to Sonnet 5 as the oracle for that step only, then drop back. Compaction/summaries: code templates in jev-only; cheapest model in jev-on; never the primary model. Measure on 5 QuixBugs + 3 ladder tasks, not the full bench.

mechanisms.name: Ensemble → normalise-dedupe → regression-prune → select, with early consensus stop (Trae Agent test-time scaling)
mechanisms.what: Trae generates N diverse patches in parallel (high-temperature sampling, multiple LLMs), normalises them (whitespace/comments) to drop duplicates, applies each and discards any that fails an existing regression test, then a selector votes with repository evidence and returns early when the first ⌈N/2⌉ votes agree.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Pruning shrank the ensemble ~28% while raising Pass@1 +5.57%; the selector added +4.08% over prompt-based picking; early consensus saves half the selection cost. It is exactly a 'code proposes, a ranker decides, tests verify' loop.
mechanisms.evidence: Trae Agent paper HTML (submitted 2025-07-31, fetched 2026-09-21): "We perform patch normalization to remove semantically irrelevant elements (such as extra spaces, line breaks, and comments) without altering program behavior"; "Patches that fail any regression test are discarded."; "The patch receiving the highest number of votes is selected as the final output. To improve efficiency, if the first ⌈N/2⌉ votes are unanimous, this consensus patch is immediately returned."; ablation at N=3: pruning +5.57% Pass@1, dedup only +3.73%, regression only +3.42%, selector agent +4.08% vs prompting-based selection, majority voting +4.14%; 75.20% Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: docs/LLM-JEV.md reports "60 % of valid extra samples duplicated sample 0" and 5 overfits: add code-level normalised dedup before Jev ranks (fewer Choice options, fewer lane test runs), run the scoped regression command in lanes as a hard filter, and let Jev's Choice be the selector with an early stop when the leading candidate's p clears the stop threshold after ⌈N/2⌉ lanes report. Jev sees the regression diff and a 'general vs test-fitting' Noul — the guard fix LLM-JEV.md asks for. Jev stays a selector (its measured strength), never a generator.

mechanisms.name: Adaptive test-time compute: branch from archived trajectories and spend more only on disagreement
mechanisms.what: SWE-Replay (Jan 2026) re-uses earlier trajectories by branching at 'critical intermediate steps' instead of restarting from scratch, choosing explore-vs-exploit without an external value model. Risa (Aug 2026) uses agreement between candidates as the router: agree → commit early, disagree → explore more, with no external judge or extra test execution at selection time.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: −17.4% cost with up to +3.8% resolution (SWE-Replay); 44.9% → 48.2% resolved with the same sampling budget (Risa). Compute goes where the run is actually uncertain.
mechanisms.evidence: SWE-Replay abstract (submitted 2026-01-29, fetched 2026-09-21): "recycling trajectories from prior trials, dynamically choosing to either explore from scratch or exploit archived experience by branching at critical intermediate steps"; "reducing costs by up to 17.4% while maintaining or even improving performance by up to 3.8%"; selection "driven by the potential and reasoning significance of repository exploration, rather than external LLM-based quality estimates". Risa https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22191 (submitted 2026-08-23, fetched 2026-09-21): "agreement at informative patch positions selects a final candidate"; "raises the macro-average resolved rate from 44.9% under uniform sampling to 48.2%"; no "external judge or selection-time test execution".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's checkpoints (state.json, steps.jsonl, decisions.jsonl) are trajectories with Jev's confidence recorded per stage. On `replan`, branch from the last checkpoint whose localisation Choice had high confidence instead of restarting; allocate extra generator samples only when Jev's top-2 gap is small, commit immediately when p ≥ stop threshold. [inference] The router decision is a Noul batch the loop already asks, so it adds no request; the saved samples are pure speed.

mechanisms.name: Speculative / eager tool execution while the model is still streaming
mechanisms.what: Start a tool as soon as its arguments finish streaming rather than after the whole step (mastra, default-on since Sept 2026; excludes approval-gated tools). PASTE predicts recurring tool calls from patterns and runs them speculatively, isolating results until the LLM confirms (−43.5% task time). Speculative programmatic tool calling only pre-launches tools annotated pure/speculatable with pure inputs and returns cached outputs if the final program actually calls them.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Removes the serial wait between generation and execution — the dominant latency in a tool loop — with correctness preserved by restricting speculation to side-effect-free actions.
mechanisms.evidence: mastra PR #24211 (opened 2026-09-16, fetched 2026-09-21): "A tool call whose arguments have finished streaming now starts running immediately, while the model is still producing the rest of the step."; enabled by default for `Agent.stream()`, disable with `eagerToolExecution: false`; excluded: "approval-gated tools, declared-suspendable tools, client-side calls, background-dispatched calls"; "Aborting a tool is a request, not a guarantee." PASTE https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18897 (submitted 2026-03-19, fetched 2026-09-21): "executes them speculatively while the LLM is still generating", "isolates speculative results until confirmed by the LLM", "43.5% reduction" in completion time, "1.8x lower" tool latency. Spec-PTC https://alexzhang13.github.io/blog/2026/spec-ptc/ (Aug 2026, fetched 2026-09-21): tools marked `speculatable=True, pure=True`; "Any speculatable tools that have dependencies that are blocked will not be speculated"; speedups only "1-1.2x" in their RLM setting.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: llm-jev already parses/anchors/compiles samples "on arrival" (LLM-JEV-DESIGN §7). Extend: the moment a `propose_fix` argument object closes in the SSE stream, apply it in a free lane and start the syntax check and the scoped test command — before the usage frame arrives. Speculate only on pure/lane-local actions (lane apply, compile, read, scoped tests in a lane); never on a workspace `run`, never on anything the risk stage could score ≥ 0.3. Jev's risk Score still gates the real commit, so Jev is not in the speculative path. Also pre-warm at step 0: `git worktree add` for lanes and test collection. Test on 3 QuixBugs programs; expect the wall win to be the generator's tail latency (77 of 228 samples hit the 20–30 s deadline in the head-to-head).

mechanisms.name: Batched reads and parallel tool calls (fewer round trips per step)
mechanisms.what: Roo's `read_file` accepts up to 100 files in one call (default 5) with a single approval; Kilo's 2026 core added parallel tool calls; Cline's context blog notes repeated single-file reads as the main redundancy source.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: A coding step that needs five files costs one model round trip instead of five; fewer turns also means fewer cache-write events and less history to compact.
mechanisms.evidence: Roo concurrent reads page (fetched 2026-09-21): "The default is 5, with a range of 1-100 files."; "The `read_file` tool automatically accepts multiple files in a single request."; "Roo asks once to read all related files together, getting the full picture immediately and providing better assistance faster." Kilo blog https://blog.kilo.ai/p/what-we-learned-from-3-million-downloads (2026-05-29, fetched 2026-09-21): shared core with "parallel tool calls, subagents, worktrees, inline diff review, sessions, and multi-model comparison"; "A missing context file becomes repeated tool calls."
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode's `read` takes one path and the OpenRouter provider sends `parallel_tool_calls: false`. Make `read` accept `paths[]` (default cap 5), and pre-load the top-k files Jev's context Nouls already select (one request over path-keyed candidates) into the first generator turn, so step 1 starts with the files in view. Allow parallel tool calls for reads only. Zero extra Jev requests; saves 1–4 generator round trips per step.

mechanisms.name: Handoff to a fresh, focused run with a code-selected file list, plus auto-compaction as the unattended fallback
mechanisms.what: Amp replaced compaction with `/handoff` (Oct 2025): analyse the thread, generate a new-thread prompt plus a list of relevant files, show it as an editable draft. Seven months later Amp Neo (May 2026) re-introduced automatic compaction at 90% and removed handoff. Goose's RPI keeps one goal per session and hands state between phases through a plan file with checkboxes so a compacted session can resume from the file.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: A fresh run with a curated file list beats stacking summaries (each compaction is lossy and 'encourages long, meandering threads'); automatic compaction is still needed for unattended runs so they never stall.
mechanisms.evidence: Amp handoff post (2025-10-23, fetched 2026-09-21): "Amp then analyzes the current thread and generates a prompt to start the new thread, along with a list of relevant files."; "The generated prompt will then appear as a draft in the new thread so you can still review and edit it before sending."; compaction "encourages long, meandering threads, in which you just compact once you run out of context window, stacking summary on top of summary". Amp Neo https://ampcode.com/news/neo (2026-05-06, fetched 2026-09-21): "When the context window fills up, Amp now compacts the thread: it summarizes the current context, starts a fresh window with that summary, and keeps going."; "Handoff is gone." Goose RPI (2026-09-21): plan file `thoughts/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm-description.md`; "goose was able to compact and pick up right where it left off because of the status updates in the plan".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode already has a persistent plan-with-evidence, `/new`, `/resume`, `-c`. Add `/handoff "<goal>"`: seed a new run with the plan, the failing-test state and the files Jev selects as still relevant (Nouls over files read/touched — no LLM needed in jev-only), pre-filled as an editable composer draft. Keep code auto-compaction at 90% for `jevcode run` / bench. Since Amp reversed course within seven months, implement handoff as a thin command over existing checkpoints rather than a new subsystem.

mechanisms.name: Reusable workflows with deterministic success checks, typed parameters and typed outputs (Goose recipes, Devin playbooks, AGENTS.md)
mechanisms.what: Goose recipes are YAML with `instructions`/`prompt`, typed `parameters` (string|number|boolean|date|file|select; required|optional|user_prompt), `extensions`, `sub_recipes` (with `sequential_when_repeated`), `response.json_schema`, and a `retry` block whose `checks` are shell commands that must exit 0, with `on_failure` cleanup. Devin playbooks are shareable prompts with Procedure/Specifications/Advice/Forbidden Actions/Required-from-User sections, created from successful sessions; Devin is migrating Knowledge into Skills (Sept 2026). A 2,853-repo study finds AGENTS.md is the interoperable context-file standard while Skills/Subagents are rarely adopted.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Makes repeated tasks runnable unattended with a code-verifiable success criterion, and gives an import format for other tools' memory/workflows.
mechanisms.evidence: Goose recipe reference (fetched 2026-09-21): `retry` with `max_retries`, `checks` (each `type: "shell"` + `command`, must exit 0), `timeout_seconds`, `on_failure`; `response.json_schema` "JSON schema for output validation"; `sub_recipes` fields `name`, `path`, `values`, `sequential_when_repeated`; parameters `input_type` one of "string", "number", "boolean", "date", "file", "select"; "Optional parameters MUST have a default value specified". Devin https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities (2026-09-21): "Turn successful sessions into reusable playbooks, or refine existing ones based on feedback"; release notes https://docs.devin.ai/release-notes (2026-09-21): 2026-09-18 "Knowledge Is Moving to Skills", 2026-06-05 "Playbooks can now specify a Devin mode". Harness study https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14690 (fetched 2026-09-21): "Context Files dominate the configuration landscape… with AGENTS.md emerging as an interoperable standard"; "Few repositories adopt advanced mechanisms such as Skills and Subagents". Kilo Memory Bank deprecated in favour of AGENTS.md (search summary 2026-09-21, secondary).
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: For the onboarding/import requirement: read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules, .roo/rules, Goose recipe YAML and playbook-style markdown into one JevCode workflow file whose `checks` (shell exit 0) are the oracle — identical to JevCode's tests-as-truth rule. Jev decides which imported instruction applies at a step (Choice with an escape option); 'Forbidden Actions' become a code denylist consulted by the risk stage, not a prompt line. Typed `response.json_schema` maps onto the structured child return in mechanism 1.

mechanisms.name: Immutable trajectory log with a derived, traceable model view and one-line step summaries
mechanisms.what: Trae records every LLM interaction, step and tool call to `trajectories/trajectory_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json` and (optionally) embeds a Lakeview one-line summary per step. OpenHands' condenser keeps the event log at full fidelity and derives the LLM 'view' (trigger at `max_size` 120 events, keep `keep_first` 4 verbatim, condense to ~60) while recording `forgotten_event_ids` so every compaction is auditable.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Debuggable runs, explainable compaction, and a human-readable transcript that stays one line per step regardless of tool-output size.
mechanisms.evidence: OpenHands condenser doc (fetched 2026-09-21): NoOp / LLMSummarizing / Pipeline / Rolling condensers; `max_size` "Event count threshold before condensation triggers (default: 120)"; `keep_first` "Number of initial events to preserve verbatim (default: 4)"; target "max_size // 2 events (default: 60)"; the Condensation event carries "forgotten_event_ids"; "logs retain full fidelity while the view is condensed". Trae README https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bytedance/trae-agent/main/README.md (2026-09-21): "automatically records detailed execution trajectories for debugging and analysis", `trajectories/trajectory_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json`, `enable_lakeview: true`, `max_steps: 200`.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: steps.jsonl / decisions.jsonl / jev.jsonl / transcript.log already are the immutable log. Add the derived-view split from COORDINATION-DESIGN §8: compaction writes a `forgotten` id list into the checkpoint so `/why` and `jevcode report` can explain what the generator no longer sees. Step summaries: code templates in jev-only (Jev picks the template via Choice, cheap), the cheap model in jev-on — never the primary model, never on the critical path (write after the step commits).

mechanisms.name: Parallel-worktree control room: cooperative vs forced stop, sleep, message-into-child, per-child meters, caps
mechanisms.what: Kilo's Agent Manager runs sessions in isolated git worktrees (or several transcripts sharing one worktree), with Cancel (cooperative) vs Stop (force), up to 20 tasks per `agent_manager` request, Multi-Version Mode capped at 4 parallel implementations, background tasks with result injection, and 'Apply to local' / PR to merge. Devin's coordinator can sleep, terminate, and message child sessions, sees per-child ACU, and queues messages delivered during long-running waits.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Gives the human exact control over parallel work (pause now vs at a safe point, kill, message, budget) without blocking the other children — the UX layer the parallel mechanisms above need.
mechanisms.evidence: Kilo Agent Manager (fetched 2026-09-21): "Multiple parallel sessions in isolated git worktrees or the shared Local workspace"; sessions in one worktree "share the same checkout, branch, and terminal state" with "separate transcripts and prompt queues"; "Cancel" sends a cooperative stop signal, "Stop" force-terminates; `agent_manager` can "start up to 20 tasks" per request; Multi-Version Mode max 4 parallel implementations; "Apply to local". Devin managed Devins https://cognition.com/blog/devin-can-now-manage-devins (2026-03-19, fetched 2026-09-21): "put child sessions to sleep or terminate them: pause or stop any managed Devin"; "Each has its own session link, so you can inspect its work or message it directly." Devin release notes (2026-09-21): 2026-08-26 "Queued Message Improvements" — messages delivered during "long-running wait"; 2026-08-12 "Side Chats". Sept-2024 MultiDevin https://cognition.com/blog/sept-24-product-update: "1 'manager' Devin and up to 10 'worker' Devins", manager "merges the changes from all successful worker Devins into one branch or pull request".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Maps onto COORDINATION-DESIGN §6–§7 (`Engine.pause({at:'step'|'now'})`, `Engine.deliver`, messaging). Expose per-child verbs in the TUI panel: pause (cooperative, next loop top — `engine.ts:965 pause()` already does this), stop (abort + lane cleanup), sleep (checkpoint + release lane), message (delivered at the child's next step), and a per-child step/wall/$ meter; cap concurrent children (≤ 4 versions of one fix, ≤ 10 children overall) and total spawned per request (≤ 20). Merge = git + Jev arbitration on conflicts only.

mechanisms.name: Cost and turn guards that are visible per call (turn caps, output spill-to-file, condense-cost line, model-flagged approval)
mechanisms.what: Goose caps turns without user input (`GOOSE_MAX_TURNS` 1000) and spills any tool response over 200,000 chars to a temp file; Kilo caps subagent `steps`; Trae caps `max_steps` 200; Roo shows the cost and before/after tokens of every condense call; Cline lets the model flag each command `requires_approval` and gates categories (safe vs all commands, project vs all files) with OS notifications when an auto-approved command runs > 30 s; Devin logs ACU-limit changes to an audit trail.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Runaway loops and giant tool outputs are the two ways a run silently burns money; per-call visibility keeps the meter honest.
mechanisms.evidence: Goose env vars (fetched 2026-09-21): GOOSE_MAX_TURNS "Maximum number of turns allowed without user input" default 1000; GOOSE_MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_SIZE "Maximum character count for a single tool response before it is written to a temporary file" default 200000; GOOSE_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD default 0.8. Roo condensing page (2026-09-21): shows "The cost associated with the context condensing AI call" with tokens before/after. Cline https://docs.cline.bot/features/auto-approve (2026-09-21): "The model marks each command with a `requires_approval` flag based on the command and arguments"; notifications "when an auto-approved terminal command has been running for 30 seconds"; YOLO mode "auto-approves everything". Devin release notes (2026-09-21): 2026-07-01 "Organization ACU limit changes are now recorded in the customer-facing audit log".
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: JevCode already has spend/step/wall/replan caps and Jev risk Scores (better than a self-flagged `requires_approval`). Add: tool-output spill (head+tail in context, full body under <runDir>/tmp, path in the transcript); a per-child cap set inherited from the parent minus spent; a one-line cost entry for every compaction/summary call in the transcript and `/cost`; the 30-s long-running-command toast. All code, no Jev.

mechanisms.name: Observability-driven harness evolution (edit the harness from trace evidence, not from vibes) — new in 2026
mechanisms.what: AHE gives every harness component a file-level representation, distils millions of trajectory tokens into a drill-down evidence corpus, and pairs every harness edit with a self-declared prediction verified against the next round's outcomes; ten iterations moved Terminal-Bench 2 from 69.7% to 77.0%, and the evolved components 'encode general engineering experience rather than benchmark-specific tuning'.
mechanisms.why_it_helps: Turns the harness itself into the thing that improves between runs, using the traces the harness already records.
mechanisms.evidence: AHE abstract (submitted 2026-04-28, fetched 2026-09-21): Component Observability "gives every editable harness component a file-level representation so the action space is explicit and revertible"; Experience Observability "distills millions of raw trajectory tokens into a layered, drill-down evidence corpus"; Decision Observability "pairs every edit with a self-declared prediction, later verified against the next round's task-level outcomes"; Terminal-Bench 2 69.7% → 77.0% over ten iterations.
mechanisms.applicability_to_jevcode: Not mission-critical and not for the speed push, but JevCode is unusually well placed: decisions.jsonl already records every Jev probability and the code rule that consumed it, and experiments/results already hold pre-registered criteria. A small offline script could propose one threshold/question-phrasing edit per round with a predicted delta and check it on the 10-task QuixBugs slice. Mark as 'later'.

speed_tricks: Eager lane apply: when a `propose_fix` argument object closes in the SSE stream, apply it in a free shadow lane and start the syntax check + scoped tests immediately, before the stream's usage frame (mastra #24211 pattern; PASTE −43.5% task time). Pure/lane-local actions only.

Normalised dedup before ranking: strip whitespace/comment differences and hash candidate patches; LLM-JEV.md says 60% of extra samples duplicated sample 0 — dedup removes those Jev options and lane test runs for free (Trae: dedup alone +3.73% Pass@1 and ~28% smaller ensemble).

Early consensus stop: return as soon as the leading candidate's Jev p clears the stop threshold after ⌈N/2⌉ lanes report (Trae's ⌈N/2⌉ unanimous rule) instead of waiting for all N samples/deadlines (77 of 228 samples hit the 20–30 s deadline in the head-to-head).

Spend samples only on disagreement: when Jev's top-2 gap is wide (p ≥ stop threshold) commit with one sample; widen to N only inside Jev's noisy 0.55–0.80 band (Risa agree→commit / disagree→explore; SWE-Replay −17.4% cost).

Branch, don't restart, on replan: resume from the last checkpoint whose localisation Choice was high-confidence (SWE-Replay branching at critical intermediate steps) — JevCode's per-step checkpoints already make this a file read.

Third cache breakpoint on the message tail (Anthropic allows 4; tools→system→messages) and constant `tool_choice`/reasoning within a phase so each step reads the growing history at 0.1× and skips prefill; surface cache-hit % in the status bar.

Stagger GLM samples on OpenRouter (sample 0, then 1..N−1) so Z.AI's automatic cache serves the later samples; verify with `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (already parsed in src/provider/openrouter.ts:273) — answers LLM-JEV-DESIGN open question #2.

Pre-warm at step 0 while Jev reads the intent: `git worktree add` the lanes, run test collection, and pre-load the top-k Jev-selected files into the first generator turn (Roo multi-file `read_file`, default 5) — step 1 starts with files in view and lanes ready.
Multi-path `read` and parallel tool calls for reads only: one round trip instead of k for context gathering; keep writes/runs serial and risk-scored.
Cheap or code-only summarisation/compaction (Kilo `compaction.model`, Trae Lakeview): never let the primary generator spend a turn on housekeeping; in jev-only use templates chosen by a Jev Choice.

Ingestion-gated context: normalise and cap tool output when it enters history (Goose spills >200k chars to a file), evict superseded file reads in batches at step boundaries, keep 2 verbatim turns — prefix stays byte-stable so cache hits survive (Cline; TokenPilot −61–87% cost).

Jev off the critical path by construction: ask the 'still-needed files' Nouls and the 'is this general' Noul in the same batch as the judge questions at the end of a step while tests run; Jev's request count stays flat (1000 questions per request already).
pitfalls: Summary stacking degrades: every harness that auto-compacts warns about cumulative loss (badlogic gist: quality 'can degrade with multiple compactions'; Amp: compaction 'encourages long, meandering threads'). Amp removed compaction (Oct 2025) then re-added it at 90% and removed handoff (May 2026) — implement handoff as a thin command over existing checkpoints, not a subsystem.

Mutating the prefix kills the cache: rewriting earlier messages, toggling `tool_choice`, changing thinking/effort params or editing tool definitions invalidates the Anthropic cache at that level and below (tool-use-with-prompt-caching table); prompts under the model minimum (1,024 tokens on Sonnet 5, 512 on Fable 5.1) are silently not cached.

Parallel samples of one prefix mostly miss the cache because the entry is written by the first request to finish — the LLM-JEV-DESIGN cost model assumes no caching, so any gain must be measured via `cached_tokens`, not assumed [inference].

Using a cheaper model for compaction is contested: Kilo allows it, Roo refuses ("Condensing always uses your active conversation provider/model") to avoid degradation with tool calls — pick one and check on 3 small tasks.

Speculative execution has side-effect risk: mastra excludes approval-gated tools and notes 'Aborting a tool is a request, not a guarantee'; discarded attempts may already have caused external effects. Speculate only on pure, lane-local, idempotent actions; never on a workspace `run` or anything the risk stage could score ≥ 0.3.

Subagent blind spots: Amp notes 'you can't guide them mid-task'; Goose forbids recursion for a reason; summary-only returns lose evidence — JevCode children must return structured facts (test results, files touched, patch hash), not prose, so Jev can judge them.

Shadow-git checkpoints slow large repos (Cline) and are disabled on nested repos (Roo); an un-ignored `.venv` or `node_modules` can make each commit expensive — reuse the existing 50 MB / DIRTY_ENTRIES_MAX 200 limits from lanes.ts.

Selection can reward test-fitting patches: Trae's regression pruning only removes patches that fail existing tests; hidden tests differ. LLM-JEV.md's 5 overfits came from the guard committing test-fitting seeds — the regression filter must be paired with the 'general vs test-fitting' Jev Noul and the evaluator remains the only truth.
Rate limits scale with parallelism: 19 GLM samples died of OpenRouter 429 in the head-to-head; caps on concurrent children/samples and the existing two-wave fallback are required, not optional.

Unverified numbers: Goose's '10 concurrent subagents (hard-coded)' comes from a third-party post, and the lead/worker turn/fallback defaults were not found on any primary Goose page — do not cite them as facts in DESIGN.md.
Closed products as references only: Devin and Amp docs describe behaviour, not code; only Goose, Cline, Roo, Kilo and Trae are inspectable (Apache-2.0/MIT) if implementation details are needed.

Kilo's 40-trillion-token lesson: 'Task size should be bounded by reviewability' — parallel children that produce more than one sitting's worth of diff waste the speed they gained; keep child scopes to one failing test or one file.

Goose's Tool Router is a preview that 'only works with Claude models served through Databricks' — a tool-search layer is not worth adopting for JevCode's six tools; Anthropic's `defer_loading` is the cache-safe equivalent if tools ever grow.
